## REQ-105 — The demo's day strip scrolls under the finger: every day in one row, five to the width, snapping to a day
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20, on the pinned /landing2 at a phone's width: "why cant i click and drag the calendar on mobile? the expierence on mobile leds itself better to that." — "do it." — and, on the first cut shown: "the boxes should render smoothly as you scroll, these fucking boxes dont render until you release".
**Found:** the day strip REQ-102 built was paged by its two arrows alone: the island's only handlers were the arrows' and the days' clicks, and the view clipped with `overflow: hidden` (no scroller), so a finger across it did nothing — reproduced on the pin at 390px: a touch swipe and a mouse drag left the strip on Oct 21; the arrow moved it to Oct 26. The first cut kept the page model — five days rendered, the group translated under the finger, the page flipped on the release — so the next days could not appear until the finger let go; its story measured 0px of scroll under a held finger.
**Requirement (read from that):** the strip is a scroller. The row holds every day the route hands down (REQ-102's 90), each a fifth of the view's width less the gaps (`grid-auto-flow: column`, `grid-auto-columns: calc((100% - 4 * 8px) / 5)`; 6px gaps on a phone); the view scrolls sideways (`overflow-x: auto`, no bar, `overscroll-behavior-x: contain`) and snaps to a day (`scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`, `scroll-snap-align: start` on each day, `scroll-padding` the focus-ring padding, so a stop is a day's edge). A finger scrolls it the way the browser scrolls anything: the boxes move under it, the next days come into view before it lets go, and it settles on a day, momentum and all; a tap is a click and picks; up and down is the page's own scroll. The arrows scroll it five days on or back from wherever it stands (`front-end/lib/day-strip.ts`: `pageTarget`, clamped to the first day and to a view of the last five; `firstOnView` reads the first day on view off the scroll, and the range beside the label and the arrows' off states follow it; a second click while the first's smooth scroll still runs goes on from where that one aimed). A mouse drags it: past a click's slack (`isDrag`, 6px) the view takes the pointer and scrolls with it, its snapping off while held (`.l2-demo__view--held`), and settles on the nearest day's stop when let go (`nearestStop`); the click a drag leaves is swallowed once, so a drag never picks the day it started on; a plain click keeps its day — the pointer is taken only once it is a drag, because taken on the press, the mouseup and the click are retargeted to the view and never reach the day. Smooth scrolling for the arrows and the settle; plain under reduced motion (the one `.l2` rule stills it). The pick by index, the summary and the booking are as REQ-102 left them; the page still never scrolls sideways. REQ-090 is amended on "a five-column grid that never scrolls" and REQ-102 on "five at a time, sliding by arrow … nothing scrolls sideways": the strip scrolls inside its view — by finger, wheel, mouse or arrow — and five stand whole on view at every stop.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/day-strip.test.ts` ("REQ-105 firstOnView — the day standing first for a scroll position", "REQ-105 pageTarget — where an arrow sends the strip", "REQ-105 nearestStop — where a let-go mouse settles", "REQ-105 isDrag — a tap is not a drag": 9 tests) · `jest/unit/landing2-page.test.ts` ("REQ-105 the demo's day strip scrolls under the finger — every day in one row, five to the width, snapping to a day": the island's import of the four rules, every day in the row, the scroller's handlers, the first day read off the scroll, the arrows' targets and off states, the mouse drag taking the pointer past the slack, the held class, the settle, the swallowed click; the stylesheet's scroller, snap, hidden bar, held rule, the row's columns, the day's snap stop, the phone's columns, reduced motion; REQ-102's bindings amended to the first day on view, the row of every day and the smooth scroll in place of the keyframe slide) · integration n/a — no backend change: a day scrolled to books through REQ-102's unchanged `POST /demo-request`, and the story books one · e2e `e2e/landing2/landing2.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-105: the demo's day strip scrolls under the finger — the boxes move as the finger moves and the next days come into view before it lets go; let go, it settles on a day; a tap picks, a short drag does not; the arrows page five from wherever it stands; a mouse drag scrolls it the same on a desktop; the day scrolled to books": the browser's own touch input through CDP at 390px, the strip read while the finger is still down, Playwright's mouse at 1280px; the REQ-090 and REQ-102 stories now read the five on view and wait for the strip at rest after an arrow).
**Evidence (2026-10-20):** RED first, the first cut — jest: the two binding tests failed and the rules' suite could not load its module; the story, run against HEAD's island and stylesheet, failed at its first swipe. GREEN, then shown, then the feedback above. RED again, the scroller — jest: `Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/day-strip'`, the amended REQ-102 bindings and the REQ-105 bindings 4 failed; the story: "the strip has scrolled under the finger before it lets go (0px)". Then GREEN: jest 16 passed; `deno check` clean; the story 3 of 3 (10–12 s), its third frame the strip mid-drag with the finger down — Oct 22 half out at the left, 23 to 26 whole, 27 coming in; REQ-090/102's three stories 3 passed. Measured on the way: (1) with the pointer taken on the press, Playwright's click on a day reached the view, not the day (pointerdown on the day; mouseup and click on the view) — hence the pointer taken only once it is a drag; (2) Chromium's tap slop on this strip ends between 15 and 18px of touch travel (8, 12 and 15px picked the day; 18px and more scrolled), and a 22px flick already carried to the next day with momentum, a step being 46px — hence the story's 19px drag at a slow pace; (3) the first cut's gate: the e2e lane failed REQ-062 (the CRM-timing flake REQ-104 noted) and, re-run, REQ-100 and REQ-046 on `locator.click: Timeout 15000ms` under the parallel load (REQ-046 in the flake ledger since 2026-10-19) — all three pass alone and none drives the strip; the scroller's first gate failed the INT lane twice on `choose-plan/int.test.ts` REQ-062 (`world.customers.length` 2, expected 1: another account's customer landed in the shared fake CRM world late, under the three lanes at once), a lane the change never touches and which passed 3 of 3 alone (288 tests, 1–2 s). Lanes in the gate at wt-show.
## REQ-106 — A paid plan pick answers at once; the CRM's customer, due and pay link come after the reply, and the person waits on a hand-off page that moves the moment the page is ready
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20: "when i click a plan in the onboarding flow the payment link takes FOREVER to load, can we speed it up and keep the exact same result in the crm? i dont care if it happens asyncronously it takes that amount of time anyway so as long as it ends up where its going fine. what i care about is that the user experience is good."
**Found:** a paid pick was one form post (`/plan/pick` → `POST /me/plan`) that waited on three CRM calls in a row — the account's customer upsert (the CRM's cold start plus its Quickbase query and insert), the first month's due, the pay link — and only then redirected to the pay page: the card sat pressed, nothing on screen, for as long as the CRM took. The CRM's work itself (REQ-054/058/059/100) was right and stays.
**Requirement (read from that):** (1) `POST /me/plan` for a paid plan replies at once: the plan is stored `pending` with the merchant account decided by the one rule (REQ-100) and no customer, due or page yet (`chosen` with the account alone; `isPreparing`), and a `pay-link` record goes on the lead outbox (`CrmLeadCapture.enqueuePayLink`, keyed apart from the sync, carrying the page the pick came from). The sweep carries it after the reply (`PayLinkMint`): the same three CRM calls, in the same order, with the same payloads as before — `CrmCustomerSync.ensure`, `raiseDue`, `mintPayLink` with the pick's account in `x-account` and the way back — and writes the result on the plan's record (`minted`), so the CRM ends up exactly where it did. A CRM that does not answer is retried by the sweep like a lead (the record reads `payLinkError: payments-unavailable` meanwhile); the CRM refusing the account by name (REQ-101, 422) is final: the record reads `merchant-unknown`, the sweep's record is cleared, the person picks again. A newer pick made while a page is being minted is never overwritten by the stale page (`samePick`): the re-marked record carries the newer pick on the sweep that follows. (2) The browser does not wait on the pick: `/plan/pick` sends a paid pick to the hand-off page `/plan/pay?back=<page>`, which reads the plan first and, when the page is already on the record (the link builder was quick), redirects straight to it — the page is never seen; otherwise it renders ("Preparing your secure payment page…", the plan's name and price, a spinner, the way back) and its island asks for the plan every second and goes to the pay page the moment it is on the record — nothing to click (without script, the page asks again every three seconds by itself); after fifteen seconds, or while the link builder is being retried, it says it is taking longer and that Resume payment waits on the cards page. A refusal by name goes back to the cards page saying why (`?plan=merchant-unknown`, as before). The wizard's and settings' plan cards show a pick being prepared as such, with the hand-off page a click away, and a refused pick as the cards again. (3) The pick's other rules stand: email first, the account decided once, the pay page carrying the way back, the receipt activating the plan, the billing a switch replaces (now carried from a pending pick too, so a change of mind before paying does not lose the billing to cancel).
**Amends:** REQ-054 and REQ-059 — the pick no longer redirects straight to the pay page; it answers pending and the hand-off page opens the page (the e2e stories pass through it); `payPageOf` is retired with its two jest tests (REQ-059's "a pending paid pick goes to its pay page" and REQ-061's "a past-due month goes to its pay page" — REQ-281): `afterPickOf` decides where a pick sends the browser, and settings reads a past-due month's page off the record as it did. REQ-099 — "only the paid pick still waits on the CRM" is retired: nothing the wizard does waits on the CRM. REQ-101 — the refusal by name arrives after the reply, read on the record and shown by the hand-off page; "nothing is stored" is now "the pick reads the refusal until the next pick".
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` ("REQ-106 plan — a paid pick is pending with its account before the CRM is reached; the page the sweep mints lands on it; a refusal is read on it; a newer pick is told apart") · `jest/unit/plan-return.test.ts` ("REQ-106 pay hand-off", 5: what a pending pick is; where a pick sends the browser; what the hand-off page does with the plan it read; the route `/plan/pay` and its island read as source — noindex, home without a session, the island polling and moving on the rules, the pick redirecting there; how the cards pages show it) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-106 choose-plan — the paid pick replies before the CRM is reached: pending, the account decided, no page yet; the sweep then makes the same customer, due and link, and the record carries the page"; REQ-054/058/059/061/062/064/100/104 re-read through `pick` — the pick plus its sweep; "REQ-101 … refused by name, nothing minted, and the pick reads the refusal until the next pick") · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-106 …", 5: the record before anything is sent and enqueuePayLink returning at once; the three calls in order and the page on the plan; a failing CRM deferred with the plan reading payments-unavailable, then minted; a name not on record final; a newer pick never overwritten by the stale page) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-106: a paid pick answers at once — the hand-off page says the payment page is being prepared, and the person lands on it the moment it is ready; the CRM holds the same customer, due and link" — the fake link builder told to take four seconds through `POST /me/plan/fake-slow`, the fake's control like fake-paid; "REQ-101: … a name not on record is refused …" amended: the refusal reaches settings through the hand-off page and the cards offer the plan again).
**Evidence (2026-10-20):** RED first — the four backend files refused type-check (38 errors: `@users/domain/coordinators/pay-link-mint/mod.ts` not found, `CrmLeadCapture` taking three arguments, `isPreparing`/`minted`/`payLinkFailed`/`samePick` not exported); jest 4 failed of 12 (`handoffOf is not a function` and the three beside it). Then GREEN — `deno test` over the plan rules, choose-plan, the sweep (unit + int), payments-link, load-profile and sign-in-landing: 85 passed, 0 failed; the plan endpoints and customer sync: 20 passed; jest plan-return (13) + dictionary consistency + welcome-steps: 57 passed; `deno check` of the six front-end files clean; `shots run e2e/plan-picker` against the worktree's server: 11 passed on the first run with the REQ-106 story red on its last line only (it compared the ACTIVE plan's payUrl, blank by REQ-061's rule, to the pay page — the assertion, not the app; now the due and customer), then 12 of 12. The first `wt-show` gate (61 stories in parallel, then the lane alone) was RED on four plan-picker stories with `page.screenshot: Timeout 90000ms exceeded` — shots screenshots after every click, and the hand-off page's island redirected by script while that screenshot was in flight (the fake mints at once, so the page was always about to leave); the route now reads the plan and redirects server-side when the page is already there, so the click lands on the pay page as before and the island only runs while the link builder is genuinely slow: 12 of 12 again on the pin, and the gate recorded by `wt-show` below. The pick itself: the story reached the hand-off page under three seconds while the link builder held the page for four, and landed on the pay page after.

## REQ-107 — The signup card says Get started, not Start free, whichever button opened it
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20, on the shipped /landing2: "if you click start on the $99 it jusmps you to start free even though you ask, just change the text to get started."
**Found:** the $99 card's Sign up (Registrarme) opens the signup card, which was titled "Start free in 30 seconds" / "Empieza gratis en 30 segundos" with a "Start free" / "Empezar gratis" button and a consent line naming that button. REQ-104 had already made the card sign up for the plan whose button brought the person to it (`data-plan`), but every word on it still said free — so a person who asked for the $99 plan read that they were starting free.
**Requirement (read from that):** the card's title, its button and its consent line say Get started — `landing2.regH` "Get started in 30 seconds" / "Empieza en 30 segundos", `landing2.sendCode` "Get started" / "Empezar", `landing2.consentA` "By tapping Get started you agree…" / "Al tocar Empezar aceptas…" — in both languages, and name no free, whichever button opened the card. The buttons INTO the card keep their own words: the nav's, the Monster Free card's, the final CTA's and the sticky bar's Start free / Empezar gratis (they sign up for Monster Free, REQ-104), the paid cards' Sign up / Registrarme. Nothing else about the card changes: the plan it signs up for is still the button's (`data-plan`), and the code still posts it. The gate's hit-target audit (REQ-344) then named the two consent boxes the consent line sits beside — 18×18 px, under the 24 px floor — so `.l2-consent input` (the signup card's and the demo's) is 26×26 now — 24 measured a hair under the floor in the judge's audit.
**Amends:** REQ-089 and REQ-104 — the card is no longer "titled Empieza gratis en 30 segundos"; the stories that read that title (REQ-089, REQ-096's heading list, REQ-097's two languages, REQ-104's two signups) read the new words.

## REQ-111 — An incomplete signup is on the CRM with everything typed so far, its selected plan and the exact stage it reached
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-21, the launch checklist: "CRITICAL — Save incomplete signups. For Monster Free, Monster, and Monster Assist, save any and all information collected, even if the customer does not complete signup. Capture contact information as early as possible so we can call and help them finish. Include their selected plan and the exact stage they reached so the team knows how to follow up. Make these incomplete signups accessible to the team."
**Found:** the contact was captured as early as it exists — the cell at send-otp (REQ-072, a lead on the CRM before the code is verified), the account's customer at verify (REQ-058/098, the outbox and its sweep), and every onboarding answer re-synced the customer (REQ-062/070) — but the customer carried no plan and no stage: a Monster Free account sat on the "Lead" rung (REQ-070's ladder had no Free rung) and nothing said how far the person got, so the team could not tell a signup that stopped at the business name from one that finished.
**Requirement (read from that):** one pure reading of where an account stands — `signupProgress` (`backend/src/users/domain/business/signup-progress/mod.ts`): the selected plan by name (Monster Free · Monster · Monster Assist; "" before a pick), where its payment stands (none · free · awaiting payment · paid · past due) and the stage in the team's words, counted over the wizard's nine questions in its order (REQ-091's one rule, `ONBOARDING_QUESTIONS`): "signed up — nothing answered yet, next the name" · "4 of 9 answered — next the state" · "3 of 9 answered — next the plan · Monster picked, awaiting payment" · "setup skipped — 2 of 9 answered, next the email" · "onboarding complete". Every CRM customer sync carries `signupPlan` ("none yet" before a pick) and `signupStage` (`CrmCustomerSync.customerFor`, reading the insurance too now), so the CRM record is written with the stage at sign-up and rewritten at every answer, the plan pick, the payment and the end of onboarding; a Monster Free account sits on a "Free" rung of the tier ladder (`tierFor`: no plan → Lead, free → Free, a pick awaiting payment → Lead, paid or past due → the plan's name); `/api/me/crm-customer` echoes both fields. The outbox's sweep carries one lane per person — the lead by its phone, the account by its id — eight lanes at once, each in order, the leads first: one account's slow CRM call (a cold start, a pay page's mint) never holds another account's stage back (the gate's parallel stories proved the one sequential sweep did: the hand-off story's 4 s mint held the stage story's sync past its wait).
**CRM side (a follow-up in theTechGoose/ppwk-crm, not this repo):** the CRM whitelists customer fields it does not declare, so `signupPlan` and `signupStage` are dropped at its door until the CRM declares them on its customer DTO and maps them to two new Quickbase Leads columns (Signup Plan, Signup Stage — the create-only `scripts/build-crm-schema.ts`, a prod step of the user's). Until then the team reads the plan and the stage in REQ-112's notice and the Free rung in Quickbase; the stage lands in Quickbase the moment the CRM declares the fields, with no change here.
**Amends:** REQ-062/070 — the customer sync's object gains the two fields and the Free rung ("Lead" was the tier of a free account).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/signup-progress/test.ts` ("REQ-111 planLabel + paymentStatus — …", "REQ-111 signupProgress — …" ×4: nothing answered; the count in the wizard's order and the Free pick; a paid pick awaiting payment; complete and skipped) · `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` (tierFor's Free rung) · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` ("REQ-111 sweep — one lane per person, carried at once: an account whose CRM call is slow never holds another account's record; a lead is on the CRM before any account is synced") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-customer-sync/int.test.ts` ("REQ-111 crm-customer-sync — the selected plan and the exact stage ride with every sync: nothing answered at sign-up, the questions as they are answered, a paid pick awaiting payment, Monster Free on the Free rung, and onboarding complete"; REQ-058/062/070's expectations carry the fields) · e2e `e2e/free-signup/free-signup.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-111: a Monster Free signup that stops after three questions is on the CRM with its plan, its stage — 4 of 9 answered, next the state — and everything typed so far").

## REQ-112 — Every signup is announced to hello@documonster.com: what happened, everything collected, the plan, the stage and the payment status
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-21, the launch checklist: "CRITICAL — Send new-signup notifications. **Found:** REQ-103's notice went once, at the account's creation, with the phone or the email, the language, the id and the time — nothing else was known yet — and nothing followed: finishing onboarding, skipping it, picking a plan and paying went unannounced.
**Requirement (read from that):** the notice says what happened — signed up · completed onboarding · skipped setup · paid — in its subject ("DocuMonster signup — completed onboarding — Monster Assist — +15125550103") and its first row, how the account was opened (by phone, by email), then the plan ("none yet" before a pick), the payment status, the stage (REQ-111's words) and every fact the account has given: the name (never the placeholder), the business, the phone, the email, the website, the address, the payment methods switched on, the insurance provider, the merchant account, the language, the sign-up and onboarded times, the user id — empty rows left out, escaped. ## REQ-113 — A paid signup carries its plan into the wizard: the $99 / $199 card's pick is made the moment the email lands, and the plan step is that plan's payment page, never the cards
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-21, the launch checklist, item 2: "Correct the signup flow for each plan — … Monster ($99) and Monster Assist ($199): Continue through the entire current signup process, including payment. **Requirement (read from that):** (1) the plan a sign-up names with the code (`POST /auth/verify-otp { plan }`; `/auth/verify` the same) is taken by `ChoosePlan.signupNamed`: free is Monster Free on record at once (REQ-104); a paid name — `monster` or `assist`, `signupPlanOf` — is kept on the account (`User.signupPlan`, written only by `UserStore.nameSignupPlan`) and picked the moment the account has the email a paid pick needs: at the code when the email is already on record, else when the wizard's email lands (`ChoosePlan.pickNamed`, called by `PUT /me` after the save) — `choose(planId, "/welcome")`: pending through primary (REQ-100), the page minted by the sweep after the reply (REQ-106), the receipt back to the wizard (`/plan/return?due=…&back=/welcome`, REQ-059); a pick already on record stands, whatever the name (REQ-104); a name that is no plan is nothing; the same email saved again picks nothing twice; a paid name with no pick yet reaches the CRM by the sweep (REQ-099). Read: the wizard's saves re-mark the account's sync record while a sweep carries it (REQ-099: a new enqueuedAt, the lease kept so the carrying sweep's `done()` sees it) — and `done()` wrote with a version check and returned silently when a save landed between its read and its write, leaving the record re-marked AND leased for `LEASE_MS` (90 s); nothing clears a lease but `done()`. `defer()` wrote blindly, overwriting a crossing save with the older mark. Both read again and write again until the write lands or the record is gone (`SETTLE_ATTEMPTS`, 8; the last write wins after that). Tests: integration `backend/src/users/domain/data/crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts` (REQ-113 ×3: `done()` with a save crossing its write — the record stays, lease cleared, the newer mark on it, due for the next sweep; `done()` after a re-mark before its read, and gone when nobody re-marked; `defer()` with a save crossing its write — the newer mark, counted once, the lease released); RED first — 2 of 3 failed as predicted ("the lease is cleared" / "the newer mark, counted once"); then GREEN — 66 passed, 0 failed over the outbox, the sweep (unit + int), the customer sync, choose-plan, the me and auth controllers (`deno test --parallel`, seven files); `shots run` with twelve workers against the restarted pin as `127.0.0.1`: 66 pass, 0 fail, and the server's log shows no deferral and no failed sweep.

## REQ-120 — No button on /landing2 changes onboarding: every sign-up lands on the wizard's plan picker and picks there
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-23: "okay now on /landing2 can you please remove the logic that changes the onboarding, everything just ends up on the plan picker onboarding page and they pick the plan there."
**Found:** two pieces of /landing2 changed the wizard by the button pressed. REQ-104: the four Empezar gratis buttons named `free` (`data-plan`), the signup island followed the last button pressed and posted the name with the code (`POST /auth/verify-otp { plan }`, `/auth/verify` the same), `ChoosePlan.startFree` stored Monster Free, and the wizard's plan step was not asked (`asksPlan`) — nine steps, the cards never shown. REQ-113: the paid cards' Registrarme named `monster` or `assist`, kept on the account (`User.signupPlan`, `UserStore.nameSignupPlan`, `ChoosePlan.signupNamed`), picked the moment the email landed (`ChoosePlan.pickNamed`, from `PUT /me`), and the plan step read that pick instead of the cards (`awaitsNamedPick`, `planStepView`: "Your plan" and the pay page, never the picker). Only /landing2 fed the mechanism — "/" and "/landing" post no plan, nor does /login — so without the buttons the whole path is dead code (REQ-281).
**Requirement (read from that):** a button on /landing2 brings the person to the signup card and nothing more; the plan is picked in onboarding, by everyone. (1) No anchor into the card carries `data-plan`; the island keeps no plan, follows no click, shows none on `#empezar`, and posts the phone and the code alone (`VerifyOtpInput` has no `plan`). The plan cards keep `data-plan` on the card itself — the id the stories read — never on the button. (2) The code stores no plan: `VerifyOtpDto` has no `plan`; `/auth/verify-otp` and `/auth/verify` call no plan logic, so a body naming one (`plan: "free"`, `plan: "monster"`) is ignored — no plan on record, nothing on the account; `PUT /me` makes no pick. `ChoosePlan.startFree`, `signupNamed` and `pickNamed`, `signupPlanOf`, `SignupPlan`, `User.signupPlan` and `UserStore.nameSignupPlan` are deleted. (3) The wizard asks its plan step of every new account — ten steps, "Pick your plan" fourth, after the email — and the step is the cards until a pick is on record (`planViewOf(plan)`, the cards when nothing is there): Monster Free picked there stores free and the wizard resumes at the state, nine steps from then on (REQ-104's `asksPlan` and REQ-059's resume rule stand, for a pick made here or in settings); a paid plan picked there goes to its pay page in this tab and the receipt brings the person back past the plan with it active (REQ-054/059/106). `awaitsNamedPick` and `planStepView` are deleted; "Your plan" and "Continue to payment" stay over a pick made from the cards. (4) The team reads the pick alone: `signupProgress.plan` is the plan on record ("" before it), the CRM's Signup Plan "none yet" and the notice's Plan row none until the picker (REQ-111/112). (5) Kept of REQ-113: `UserStore.update` takes the name, the email and the language only — the admin flag, the onboarding stamp and any other field a PUT /me body carries are dropped — and the outbox's settling writes.
**Amends:** REQ-104 — the carry with the code and the nine-step wizard are retired; "never meets the credit card ask" stands as the picker's Monster Free card (free is stored without a card, REQ-054); its two stories are replaced by this requirement's. REQ-107 — the card's words stand; "the card still signs up for the plan whose button opened it" is retired, its story amended. REQ-111 — a sign-up's plan is the pick on record alone; its story picks Monster Free in the wizard before it stops. REQ-113 — retired, but (4) the PUT /me guard and the outbox's settling writes (its three outbox tests stand). REQ-119 — "no sign-up names it with the code" is moot: no sign-up names any plan.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/welcome-steps.test.ts` ("REQ-120 nothing from /landing2 changes the wizard's plan step: it is the cards until a pick is made there", 2: the rules know no named plan; the wizard shows the cards until a pick is on record and reads a pick as it stands, the front-end carrying no sign-up plan) · `jest/unit/landing2-page.test.ts` ("REQ-120 no button on /landing2 names a plan: the card posts the phone and the code alone", 2: the four buttons into the card carry no plan, the cards keep their id; ## REQ-121 — Onboarding resumes with only the unanswered questions: a later login never re-asks a question the account has already answered
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-23: "we should not ask the onboarding questions that we already have an answer to on next login, if you login and have not completed question it should show only questions that have not been answered."
**Found:** the wizard (front-end/islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx) listed every step the account was asked at all (REQ-104's `askedSteps`: all of them, minus the plan once Monster Free was on record), started at the FIRST open one (`firstIncomplete`) and then walked every later step, answered or not: a person who skipped the business name and came back met the business name, then the email, the state, the address, the payment methods, the logo and the insurance again, each already filled in, and the progress read "Step 2 of 10". Where a code lands is REQ-091's and was right: the wizard while any question is open, the dashboard once none is.
**Requirement (read from that):** (1) Every visit to the wizard asks the questions that have no answer on record when it opens — in the wizard's order, by REQ-091's one definition of answered (`isAnswered`, shared/quote-flow/onboarding-questions.ts) — and then the closing sample-quote screen, which is education, not a question; a question answered on an earlier visit is never shown again, and the progress counts those steps alone ("Step 1 of 3" for two open questions). The list is fixed when the wizard opens: answering a step on this visit does not pull it out from under the person. (2) A brand-new account, nothing answered, meets all ten steps as before (REQ-120). (3) REQ-059's resume stands over that list: back from a pick (`/welcome?after=plan`) the wizard lands on the first OPEN step after the plan's slot in the registry — the last step when none is — never on an earlier question the person skipped on the way to the plan. (4) REQ-104's rule folds into this one: the plan step is open until a pick is on record — none, or a paid pick still on its pay page, keeps it — and Monster Free, or an active paid plan, closes it; `asksPlan`, `askedSteps` and the registry's `asked` hook are deleted with `firstIncomplete`, replaced by `openSteps` (front-end/lib/welcome-steps.ts). The wizard's "✓ plan active" line goes with them: a plan on record active is answered, so no visit shows that step.
**Amends:** REQ-091 — "render the wizard, at the first open question" stands; the questions after it are the open ones alone. REQ-104 — "never shown the cards again" stands as "the plan is answered"; its unit tests are rewritten over `openSteps`. REQ-059 — the resume past the plan stands, over the open steps. REQ-120 — the ten-step wizard stands for a new account; its welcome-steps unit tests are amended to the new exports.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/welcome-steps.test.ts` ("REQ-121 the wizard asks only the questions still open, and resumes past the plan over those", 3: the open steps are the unanswered questions in order plus the closing screen, a pending pick open and a free or active plan closed; the resume after a pick lands on the first open step after the plan's slot; the wizard is bound to the rule — `openSteps` at mount, index 0 or `indexAfterPlan`, no `firstIncomplete`, no `asked`) · integration: n/a — no backend change; where a code lands is REQ-091's, untouched, and the rule is the wizard's own · e2e `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-121: a later login asks only the questions still open — with the business name and the logo left open the wizard is three steps, the business name, the logo and the sample quote; the seven answered are never shown again, and a brand-new account still meets all ten").
**Evidence (2026-10-23):** RED first — `npx jest unit/welcome-steps.test.ts`: 4 failed of 6 (the module exported `askedSteps`/`asksPlan`, `openSteps` was not a function); `shots run e2e/onboarding-until-answered` against the pin (localhost:5302, this worktree): REQ-121's story failed — the page never showed "Step 1 of 3" (the wizard opened at the business name as "Step 2 of 10" and walked on to the email, already answered). Then GREEN — `deno task test:unit` rc 0: deno 608 passed, jest 64 suites, 641 passed, 1 skipped; `deno check` clean on welcome-steps.ts, WelcomeWizard.tsx and welcome.tsx; `deno lint` clean on the seven touched source and story files; `shots run` against the pin over onboarding-until-answered, free-signup and plan-picker: REQ-121's story passed (three steps, "Step 1 of 3" … "Step 3 of 3", no answered question between), REQ-091's two stand, and six stories were amended to the rule they had encoded the other way: REQ-120's "Step 4 of 9" after Monster Free is "Step 1 of 6" (the six questions still open), and the five plan-picker stories that sign in with the name and the email on file (REQ-054 ×2, REQ-100, REQ-106, REQ-119) no longer press Continue on a prefilled email step — the wizard goes from the business name to the plan. On the way, REQ-058's story read the CRM straight after the name's save and found "unknown dragon mcdragonson" once under an idle box (the sweep writes the record after the reply, REQ-098 — the same read REQ-062's story already repeats); its three reads poll the record now, 10 s at most, and the story passed on the rerun (12 of 13 plan-picker stories; REQ-101's /plan/test story, untouched, hit shots' 90 s screenshot cap once on that rerun after passing twice earlier). The first `wt-show` gate (unit and int green, 68 of 69 stories green under its own server) refused on one more story that had encoded the re-asking — REQ-080's "Subscribe fires …" in e2e/meta-pixel, the same prefilled-email Continue at two sites, meta-pixel being a file the pin runs had not covered; amended the same way, it passed against the pin. The gate's result on the requirement is in the merge receipt.

## REQ-122 — /contact honors ?lang= like the legal pages, the consent sentence names no phone number, and a page is labelled the language it paints
**Source:** RingCentral's TCR reviewer (case 32804924, emails of 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21, forwarded by Hans on 2026-10-22): "Update your Privacy Policy and SMS Terms links to the English-specific URLs: https://documonster.com/privacy?lang=en, https://documonster.com/sms-terms?lang=en" — "TCR reviewers specifically check the English version to verify compliance" — and "If using the web form at https://documonster.com/contact, please remove the phone number reference." Raphael, 2026-10-27, on the explanation of that thread: "fix the code only fixes and then the hans fixes give to me in a list."
**Found:** (1) The four legal pages read `?lang=` (REQ-066's `legalHandler`: the pick persisted to `pm_lang`), but `/contact` read only the cookie, then `pickLangFromAcceptLanguage` — which returns Spanish for everyone (REQ-043 amendment) — so `https://documonster.com/contact?lang=en` was the Spanish form for a reviewer with no saved language (verified live: `<title>Contáctanos`, h1 "Ponte en contacto"); the bare `/privacy` and `/sms-terms` are Spanish for the same visitor, which is what the reviewer saw. (2) The consent sentence (`contactPage.smsConsent`, REQ-068) said "Reply HELP to 855-362-8666 for assistance" — HELP is a keyword replied to the texting number; a voice line in the opt-in language is the phone number reference a TCR reviewer flags. (3) The app shell (`routes/_app.tsx`) labelled `<html lang>` from the browser's Accept-Language on every page but the two landings, while the legal pages and `/contact` paint Spanish regardless of it — so an English browser got a Spanish page labelled English (verified live: `<html lang="en">` over "Política de privacidad"), which also keeps the browser from offering to translate it.
**Requirement (read from that):** (1) ONE resolver of a public page's language, `resolvePageLang(req)` (`front-end/lib/page-lang.ts`): an explicit `?lang=en|es` wins and is the pick to persist, then the visitor's saved `pm_lang` (HTTP/2 comma-joined cookies included), then Spanish — the browser's Accept-Language ignored on purpose, as before; a `?lang=` that is no language falls through. (2) ONE GET handler for the public pages, `publicPageHandler` (`front-end/lib/public-page.ts`, REQ-066's `legal-page.ts` renamed and retired, REQ-281): it resolves the language, persists a pick to `pm_lang` for a year as every language pick in the app is, and hands the page `{ lang }`; `/terms`, `/refund-policy`, `/privacy`, `/sms-terms` AND `/contact` export it, so `/contact?lang=en` is the English form — "Get in touch", the English consent sentence — labelled English, the pick sticking on the bare path; `/contact?lang=es` the Spanish one; a bare `/contact` with nothing saved stays Spanish-first. (3) The handler records the language on `ctx.state.lang` and the app shell labels `<html lang>` with it before its own guess, so a page is labelled the language it paints: a bare `/privacy`, `/sms-terms` or `/contact` on an English browser is `<html lang="es">` over Spanish; the `?lang=en` links are `<html lang="en">` over English on any browser. (4) The consent sentence names no phone number in either language: "You may reply STOP to opt out at any time. Reply HELP for assistance. Messages and data rates may apply. Message frequency will vary." / "Puede responder STOP en cualquier momento para darse de baja. Responda HELP para obtener ayuda. Pueden aplicarse tarifas de mensajes y datos. La frecuencia de los mensajes variará." — the `{phone}` placeholder and the route's substitution are gone; the "Prefer to talk?" line under the form and the footer's number (REQ-044) stay.
**Amends:** REQ-066 — the shared handler is the public pages' (`publicPageHandler`), not the legal pages' alone. REQ-068 — the consent sentence's HELP clause names no number; the story's expected sentence follows.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/contact-english.test.ts` ("REQ-122 resolvePageLang — ?lang= wins and is the pick, then pm_lang, then Spanish; the browser's language never" ×5; "REQ-122 /contact is a public page like the four legal pages, and its consent sentence names no phone number" ×4: both dictionaries; the contact route on the handler with no phone handed to the sentence; the four legal routes on the same handler and `legal-page.ts` gone; the shell reading `ctx.state.lang`) · integration n/a — a route's language resolution, a shell attribute and two strings, no backend · e2e `e2e/contact-english/contact-english.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-122: /contact?lang=en is the English form for a visitor with no saved language — the consent sentence says Reply HELP for assistance and names no phone number — the pick sticks on /contact, ?lang=es flips it back, and a bare /contact on an English browser stays Spanish-first, labelled Spanish"; "REQ-122: the two links the TCR submission names open the English documents, labelled English, for a visitor with no saved language — and the bare links stay Spanish, labelled Spanish") · `e2e/legal-pages/legal-pages.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-068's story reads the amended sentence).
**Evidence (2026-10-27):** RED first — the stories against the worktree's server on the pin (`shots run`, localhost:5280): `the page never showed "Get in touch"` at /contact?lang=en (the Spanish form, 27 s); and with the shell's `ctx.state.lang` reverted, both stories: `the server itself labels the Spanish form Spanish for an English browser — expected "es", got "en"`; jest under the same revert: the shell assertion failed (1 failed, 8 passed — its first form matched the comment, tightened to the expression). Then GREEN — jest contact-english + support-contact: 13 passed; `shots run` on the restarted pin, contact-english + legal-pages: 8 pass, 0 fail (REQ-068's story on the amended sentence among them); `deno check` on the nine touched front-end files and `deno lint` clean. On the way: a stored pick (`pm:lang`) is mirrored back into the cookie on the next load (lib/lang.ts), so the story forgets localStorage as well as the cookie between visits; the full-suite run on the pin (70 stories, twelve workers) failed REQ-108's demo story once on a 10 s locator timeout and it passed alone (3.9 s) — this change touches nothing it drives.
**The gate's find (2026-10-27):** the first `wt-show` gate — unit and int green, the e2e lane 135 s against its last green 42 s — refused on REQ-056's story alone, "the page never showed Monster is active" (69 of 70 green). Its transcripts: the pick (`POST /api/me/plan`) answered `pending` with no due yet — REQ-106 mints the CRM's customer, due and pay link by the sweep AFTER the reply — the story's `fake-paid` a breath later answered 404 "plan-missing: nothing to pay", and the `refresh` after it found the due minted but unsettled, so the plan stayed pending. The only story that pays by the fake's remote control without going through the hand-off page (which waits for the page) now reads the plan until its due is on it (`untilDue`, 20 s at most) and asserts the fake answers 200 before it looks at /settings — isolation, not a re-run (REQ-384).

## REQ-123 — Every email leaves from documonster.com: nothing via monsterrg.com
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-27: "i do not want to SEND ANYTHING VIA monsterrg.com can we send everything via documonster instead?"
**Found:** the From was whatever `POSTMARK_FROM` the process carried, and three were in play — none of them documonster.com (the Postmark outbound log of server ai-testy-1234, read 2026-10-27): `warnings@monsterrg.com` (1,414 mails — every box's env sets it, so the gate's e2e runs and the dev pins: the stories' login codes and the `[contact]`/`[demo]`/`[call]` notices to the team inbox), `noreply@quotejefe.com` (202 — prod on Deno Deploy: the real login codes and REQ-103's signup notices), `rafac@monsterrg.com` in main/.env (read by nothing: the box env wins); and the paperwork alias domain was `paperworkmonster.com` in code (`<alias>@paperworkmonster.com`, which REQ-085 had left as "a name"). documonster.com is a verified Postmark domain (pm-bounces CNAME to pm.mtasv.net; two probes from it on 2026-10-22 were accepted). `ai@monsterrg.com` (106, the daily "Replay Voicemail Report") is another app on the same Postmark server, not this one.
**Requirement (read from that):** every email this app sends leaves from documonster.com, and no env var has a say. One module (`backend/src/communication/domain/business/sender/mod.ts`) owns it: `SEND_DOMAIN` = documonster.com; the house From `"DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>` for everything that is not a contractor's paperwork (login codes, the team's contact/demo/call notices, the signup notices); a contractor's paperwork from `<emailAlias>@documonster.com` (roadmap p.7's alias, unchanged) or `noreply@documonster.com` with none on file. `EmailService` builds Postmark's payload with the pure `postmarkPayload()` (no From → the house From) and refuses any From off documonster.com before dev mode or the key are looked at. `POSTMARK_FROM` is retired — deleted from the code, the smoke tests and the contact tests; the Deno Deploy variable is inert and `.wt/prod.md` deletes it. The team inbox's monsterrg.com addresses stay: that is where mail lands, not where it leaves from.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communication/domain/business/sender/test.ts` ("REQ-123 sender — every email leaves from documonster.com: the house From is DocuMonster <hello@documonster.com>, a business alias is <alias>@documonster.com, noreply@documonster.com without one, and any other domain is refused") · `backend/src/communication/domain/data/email-service/test.ts` ("REQ-123 postmarkPayload — a send with no From leaves as DocuMonster <hello@documonster.com>; a From on documonster.com stands", "REQ-123 EmailService — a From off documonster.com is refused before anything else happens: not in dev mode, not with a key") · `jest/unit/sender-domain.test.ts` (4: the constants; no tracked source reads POSTMARK_FROM; none names an address on the old sender domains; monsterrg.com named only where mail lands) · int `backend/src/communication/domain/data/email-service/int.test.ts` ("REQ-123 EmailService int — the login code's email reaches Postmark from DocuMonster <hello@documonster.com>, not from the POSTMARK_FROM in the process env") · `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/int.test.ts` ("REQ-123 send-paperwork-email: a quote leaves from <alias>@documonster.com — the business name's slug — and from noreply@documonster.com with no business identity on file") · e2e n/a — the From line is Postmark's payload, no page shows it · smoke, on demand and never in the gate: `backend/src/communication/domain/data/email-service/smk.test.ts` ("REQ-123 smoke (real Postmark): DocuMonster <hello@documonster.com> and <alias>@documonster.com are accepted senders" — two probes to Postmark's blackhole address).
**Evidence (2026-10-27):** RED first — `deno test` over the four backend files: TS2307 `sender/mod.ts` not found, TS2305 `postmarkPayload` not exported; jest: "Cannot find module '../../backend/src/communication/domain/business/sender/mod'". GREEN — `deno test` over the six touched backend files: 26 passed, 0 failed; jest unit `sender-domain`: 4 passed (old-origin and brand-name still pass); `deno check` and `deno lint` clean on the changed files; the smoke file with the real key (`--env-file`): 6 passed, the real probe accepted both `"DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>` and `sender-probe@documonster.com` (Postmark returned a MessageID for each, 568 ms).

## REQ-127 — An upgrade charges the difference, a downgrade refunds nothing, and the plan lives on a Billing tab that says plainly what the person is on
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02, on Alex: "i see alex paid $99, it seems that he picked the wrong plan, but when he upgrades its trying to charge him 399 not 300 for the difference." Then: "fix the proration problem. upgrade charges the difference, downgrade has no refund, rework the pan ui so that its SUPER clean what plan the user is on. right now its pretty confusing. how about just a billing tab rather than a slot on the page."
**Found:** a switch of paid plan was a fresh pick: `PayLinkMint` raised the new plan's full first month (`pricing.priceCents` — $399 for Monster Assist+) and the old $99 billing ran until the new one was live (REQ-061); no requirement from REQ-054 to REQ-119 said a word about a credit. On /settings the plan was one panel among nine, its state a sentence ("Monster is active since 2026-10-20 · next bill 2026-11-20").
**Requirement (read from that):** ONE pure rule, `shared/quote-flow/plan-switch.ts` `switchQuote(current, targetId, now)`, read by the backend and drawn by the page: (1) UPGRADE — from an ACTIVE monthly plan to a dearer one: the due is the difference of the two list prices (Monster → Monster Assist+ = $300), its memo names both plans, and once it settles the new billing runs at the new plan's full price a month after activation, the old billing canceled as before; (2) DOWNGRADE — from an active monthly plan to a cheaper one: nothing is charged and nothing refunded; the plan switches NOW, the old billing is canceled and the new one starts at the cheaper price on the day the old one would have billed next (`firstBillAt`), so the paid month is kept and no month is charged twice; (3) everything else is a first pick at full price as before: from free, from a pending pick, from past due, to or from the one-time test tier; back to free is REQ-056/061 unchanged (billing stops, no refund). The pending record carries what its due is for (`dueCents`, `switchedFrom`), a downgraded record carries `firstBillAt`. (4) The Billing tab: /settings is two tabs, Account (everything that was there) and Billing (`?tab=billing`, where a pick and a receipt come back to — `pageAfterPick("/settings")`, and where `?plan=` errors show). Billing reads, in this order: the plan's name in large type with its price per month, one status pill (Active · Payment pending · Past due · Free · Preparing), then the facts — next bill, card on file, member since — then the action a pending or past-due plan needs (Pay now / Resume payment / Open the payment page), then "Change plan": the other plans as cards, each with ONE line saying exactly what picking it does — "Upgrade · $300 today, then $399/month", "Downgrade · nothing today · $99/month from Nov 20, 2026", "Back to free · billing stops today · no refund", "$99/month · first month today" — in both languages.

## REQ-128 — A record that reaches the lead outbox while a sweep is in flight is carried at once, not after that sweep
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02, on REQ-127's note that the REQ-060 story fails when the plan-picker stories run together: "can you please fix it?"
**Found:** `CrmLeadCapture.kick()` only flagged `again` when a sweep was in flight, so a new record waited for the whole sweep to finish — and one sweep carries every lane, including a pay-link mint the REQ-106 story slows by 4 s (`fake-slow`). REQ-060's phone lead, enqueued while that mint held the sweep, landed ~4 s late, after the story's "left" moment: `made when the phone was typed, before the person left (…:24.698Z < …:20.973Z)`. In production the same shape: a lead typed during a slow CRM cold start waits behind it. The leases (REQ-072) already keep two sweeps off one record, and `claim` is a KV atomic check — so there was never a reason for a second pass to wait.
**Requirement (read from that):** a record enqueued while a sweep is in flight is carried NOW by a pass of its own, started beside the sweep over whatever is due and unclaimed (the leases keep the two off one record); a record that pass finds held by the sweep (REQ-099's re-mark) is still swept right after it. `drain()` still joins the sweep in flight (REQ-072 as it was); `idle()` waits for the sweep, the passes and the follow-up.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` (the REQ-098 case as it was: a record that arrives while the sweep is on its list gets its own pass, no third one when nothing was held) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-128 a record enqueued while a sweep is held by a slow one is carried at once, not after it") · e2e the REQ-060 story, which this makes stable alongside REQ-106's slow mint.

## REQ-129 — A subscription charges the full price the day it is picked, a prorated amount on the 1st of the next month, and the full price on every 1st after that
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02: "subscriptions should charge $399 whenever it happens, then on the 1st of the month prorated then every month $399."
**Found:** REQ-061 billed a calendar month after activation at the full price, forever on the activation's day of the month (picked Nov 20 → billed the 20th); the CRM's subscription (ppwk-crm REQ-081) knew one amount.
**Requirement (read from that):** the pay page collects the full month on the day of the pick, as before; that pays the plan through a calendar month later (`paidThrough`, Nov 20 → Dec 20). The billing then anchors to the 1st: the first bill falls on the 1st of the following month (Dec 1, 00:00 UTC) for the days of that month past `paidThrough` at the month's rate — Dec 20–31 is 12 of 31 days, $399 × 12/31 = $154 (rounded to the cent); every 1st after that is the full price. A pick on the 1st pays through the next 1st, so its "prorated" bill is the full month. A SWITCH (REQ-127) keeps the anchor: the new billing's first bill is the day the old one would have billed next (the next 1st), prorated at the new price if the old billing had not yet collected its first bill, the full new price otherwise. One pure rule in `shared/quote-flow/plan-switch.ts` (`anchoredSchedule`, `switchedSchedule`), read by the backend and drawn by the Billing tab: "Next bill · Dec 1, 2026 · $154 (prorated)", then "$399". The CRM takes the first bill's own amount (`firstAmountCents`, ppwk-crm REQ-125) and says what the next bill is for (`nextAmountCents`); this app's real client sends it, the fake bills it. The card's note for a first pick says the whole shape: "$399 today · prorated on the 1st · then $399/month".
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/plan-switch.test.ts` ("REQ-129 …": the 1st of the next month; the prorated first bill from paidThrough — Nov 20, the 1st, Jan 31; a switched schedule before and after the first collection) · `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` ("REQ-129 settle marks what the first month pays through; the switch records carry it") · `jest/unit/billing-tab.test.ts` (the next-bill fact carries the amount and the prorated word; the first-pick note) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-129 choose-plan — the first settled month starts the billing on the 1st of the next month for the days past paidThrough, then the full price every 1st"; the REQ-061 and REQ-127 cases amended to the anchored schedule) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` (the REQ-127 story: the next bill is the 1st with its prorated amount; the first-pick note).
**Also:** the fake clock the stories drive (`POST /me/plan/fake-bill`) bills that person's subscription alone — anchored to the same 1st, one story's "a month on" billed every other story's subscription too. The CRM's side is ppwk-crm REQ-125 (`firstAmountCents` / `nextAmountCents`), deployed before this.
**Evidence (2026-11-02):** `deno task test:unit` 619 passed (deno) + jest 679 passed / 1 skipped · `deno task test:int` 312 passed · `shots run e2e/plan-picker` 14/14 three times · `shots run e2e` 74 passed / 0 failed · `deno lint` on the touched directories: the one problem is in an untouched file (crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts, at HEAD).

## REQ-130 — A developer service token that opens a session for an existing user, skipping the OTP
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02: "Mint a developer token and put it as an environment variable and use it as your login. If you have this developer token, it skips the authorization feature. Test this locally before you deploy it to prod." (To impersonate Alex on prod and confirm his upgrade link is $300, an automation identity needs a session without the OTP that only reaches a phone.)
**Found:** The only ways into a session are the OTP (texted to a phone, never returned on the deploy, master `000000` hard-disabled in prod) or a KV/bootstrap secret not set in the automation's shell. No service-credential path minted a session the way a service account would.
**Requirement (read from that):** `POST /auth/dev-login { token, phoneNumber }` mints a real session for the EXISTING, live user who owns the phone and sets the `pm_session` cookie — skipping the OTP — but ONLY when the server's `DEV_LOGIN_TOKEN` env var is set and the presented token matches it (constant-time compare). Unset (the default) the endpoint is hard-closed in dev AND prod, so nothing is exposed by accident — stricter than BootstrapSuperAdmin, which is open in local dev. It never creates an account and refuses a closed one (404). This is the automation-identity path (like a service account), not a person typing a one-time code. `DevLogin` coordinator holds the gate (`isAllowed`) and the mint (`byPhone`); the AuthController endpoint maps its errors to 403 (`forbidden`) / 404 (`no_user`).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/dev-login/test.ts` ("REQ-130 …" ×4: hard-closed when the env var is unset even with a token presented; a wrong token rejected and only the exact one accepted; `byPhone` mints a plain (non-impersonation) session for the existing user; forbidden without the gate, 404 for a phone with no live user, 404 for a closed account) · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/dev-login.int.test.ts` ("REQ-130 …": over HTTP — 403 when the server token is unset, 403 on a wrong token, 404 for an unknown phone, 200 + cookie + session that resolves on `/me` for the real thing) · e2e n/a — a service-credential endpoint with no user-facing UI; the OTP login flow's e2e is unchanged.
**Evidence (2026-11-02):** RED first — the int test hit the unwired route and got 404 where the gate must 403 (`-404 / +403`). Then GREEN after wiring the coordinator, DTO (`parseDevLogin`), endpoint and module registration: `dev-login/test.ts` 4 passed; `dev-login.int.test.ts` 1 passed; full lanes and the local real-server check below.

## REQ-131 — A paid due activates its plan whenever the payer comes back, and even after a re-pick buried it
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02, on Alex (A2Z Landscape LLC): "So that's messed up. Can you give it a look and figure out why the hell it never logged Alex's payment?" / "fix it."
**Found (prod logs + git, 2026-11-02):** NMI approved Alex's $99 sale at 15:53:22 (txn 12756989241, due 8ffef1b7); the receipt had him on `/plan/return` at 15:53:28; the CRM posts a charge's settlement by a deferred outbox job (its REQ-113) and that job finished at 15:53:55 — so the ONE best-effort `POST /me/plan/refresh` the return page makes read the due still open, `settle()` left the plan pending, and nothing in v2 ever asked again: no retry, no callback, no sweep re-check. He re-picked three times; `choose()` treated a pick-while-pending as a first pick (`switchQuote` only knows switches from ACTIVE plans) and wrote a new pending record with a new unpaid due each time, orphaning the paid one and re-syncing the CRM tier to Lead. His link read $399.
**Requirement (read from that):** a minted due is WATCHED until it settles. `CrmCaptureOutbox.addSettleWatch` is a `settle-watch` record of its own (`["crm-capture","settle-watch",userId]`: the due, the pick it was minted for, a 48 h `watchUntil`; re-marked like the pay-link record, a held lease kept) — written by the sweep right after `PayLinkMint` puts the page on the record, and re-marked by `ChoosePlan.refresh` whenever `/plan/return` reads the due still open. `SettleWatch.check` asks the CRM (`dueOpen`) and writes what the pure `watchOutcome` says: open → `waiting` (the sweep defers it on its backoff, never an error — an unpaid page is the ordinary case); settled and the record still carries the due → the pick active (`settle`); settled but a later UNPAID first pick replaced the record → the paid pick restored active (no page to resume); settled and the plan is active/free/gone, or the record is a SWITCH from the paid plan (`switchedFrom`) → nothing. On activation the tier (REQ-062/099) and the paid notice (REQ-112) ride the outbox as they do from `refresh`; `refresh` activating the plan drops the watch. A window passed unpaid ends the watch, the plan as stored. The repair is the same code path: `POST /admin/users/:id/settle-watch { dueId, planId, merchant? }` (super admin only) enqueues that watch for a due the CRM holds, so Alex's $99 restores Monster active over the $399 pick and his next upgrade pick is the $300 difference (REQ-127) — never a hand edit of KV. The fake's `POST /me/plan/fake-paid { quiet: true }` settles the due without telling the app, so a story can watch the sweep do it.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` ("REQ-131 plan — watchOutcome …" ×3: open waits / settled activates the pick carrying the due; a later unpaid pick replaced it → the PAID pick restored; nothing when active already, back to free, gone, or an upgrade from the paid plan) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/data/crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts` ("REQ-131 outbox — addSettleWatch …": keyed apart, the pick and the 48 h window on it, a re-mark restarts the clock and keeps a held lease, defer keeps the pick, done clears it) · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-131 the page minted, the sweep watches its due …": the watch is on the outbox the moment the page is; open → waiting with backoff and no error; settled → active, the paid notice mailed, the tier revised; "REQ-131 a watch whose 48 h window passed …": cleared, the plan as stored) · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-131 choose-plan — a due paid while nobody presses anything …": active by the sweep, tier Monster, billing started; "… an unpaid due keeps its watch waiting …"; "… Alex: the paid pick buried under a later unpaid first-month due is restored … the upgrade then charges the difference ($300), never $399"; "… /plan/return reading the due settled drops the watch") · `backend/src/users/entrypoints/admin-controller/settle-watch.int.test.ts` ("REQ-131 POST /admin/users/:id/settle-watch …": 403 for the account itself, 400 without the plan, 200 + the sweep restores Monster active over the $399 pick, the upgrade is 30000 from monster) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-131: paid on the page and the receipt tab closed — no return, no refresh — the plan is active within the sweep's minute, by itself").
**Evidence (2026-11-02):** RED first — `plan/test.ts`: `The requested module './mod.ts' does not provide an export named 'watchOutcome'`; `crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts`: `outbox.addSettleWatch is not a function`; the coordinator, sweep and admin files: `Module not found ".../settle-watch/mod.ts"`. One real find on the way: the first green run of REQ-132's "pick while pending" story failed once under the sweep's timing — the Monster watch, still on the outbox after `refresh` activated the plan, read the new UPGRADE record as "a later pick that buried the paid one" and wrote Monster back over it; hence the `switchedFrom` guard in `watchOutcome` (unit-tested) and `dropSettleWatch` on activation (int-tested), after which the choose-plan file passed 3×3 runs. GREEN: `deno check` + `deno lint` on the touched files clean (the one lint finding, `require-await` on `crossed` in the outbox int test, is at HEAD too); `deno task test:unit` → `626 passed | 0 failed` + jest `679 passed`; `deno task test:int` → `323 passed | 0 failed`; e2e on the host (`SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check --filter REQ-131`) → `✓ REQ-131: paid on the page and the receipt tab closed … · 57.5s`, `1 pass · 0 fail`. The prod repair of Alex's account and his $300 link: below, under REQ-132's evidence.

## REQ-132 — A pick while a pick is pending asks the CRM first, and the same plan picked again is the same page
**Source:** the same find (REQ-131): Alex's three re-picks each minted a new unpaid due over the paid one.
**Requirement (read from that):** `ChoosePlan.choose` on a record that is pending with a due calls `refresh` first (best effort: a CRM that does not answer leaves the record as stored and REQ-131's watch restores the paid pick later), so a due paid a moment ago makes the pick a SWITCH from the plan it paid for — an upgrade charges the difference (REQ-127) — never a second first pick written over it. And the SAME plan picked again through the same merchant account while its page is pending (minted, or being minted by the sweep) is answered with that record: no second due, no second link; a different plan, or a pick after the CRM's final `merchant-unknown`, is a new pick as before.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the rule is the coordinator's order of calls, exercised on the fakes · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-132 choose-plan — a pick while a pick is pending asks the CRM first …": paid Monster then Assist+ picked without any refresh → pending upgrade, dueCents 30000, switchedFrom monster, the CRM's dues 9900 + 30000, and a later sweep never writes Monster back; "REQ-132 choose-plan — the same plan picked again while its page is pending is the same page": same dueId/payUrl/chosenAt, one due and one link on the CRM; a different plan is a new due) · e2e n/a — the existing REQ-054/055/059/127 stories cover the pick and the pay page; the re-pick is API-level and covered above.
**Evidence (2026-11-02):** RED with the REQ-131 files above (`Module not found` on the sweep's new dependency), then the "pick while pending" story itself red once for the watch race described under REQ-131. GREEN in the same runs: choose-plan int file `59 passed | 0 failed` ×3, `deno task test:int` `323 passed | 0 failed`.

## REQ-133 — No business logic on the front end: a pending plan is read against the CRM by the backend itself, the CRM says when a due settles, and the return page only redirects
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-02: "Why wouldn't you just do that on the back end instead of the refresh should never affect something like this? The front end should never affect the back end." / "The front end should not be doing any business logic, only presentation logic. Put all of that in the back."
**Found:** REQ-131's watch made activation the backend's, but two things still hung off a page: `/plan/return` pressed `POST /me/plan/refresh` (a state change driven by a page load), and that press re-marked the watch to shorten its backoff — a UI action tuning backend polling. The watch itself backed off to five minutes between looks.
**Requirement (read from that):** (1) `POST /me/plan/refresh` is gone — `planClient.refresh` with it. `ChoosePlan.current` is the one read: a pending plan with a due is read against the CRM (`settledOnRead` — settled → active on that read, the watch dropped, the tier and the paid notice ride the outbox; open → as stored; a CRM that does not answer → as stored), the way an active plan is read against its billing (`projected`). `choose` on a pending pick reads the same way (REQ-132). (2) `/plan/return` is a redirect that only READS the plan, to know which pixel the landing page fires (REQ-080). (3) The watch looks at a fixed cadence — `WATCH_EVERY_MS` 55 s, a shade under the sweep's minute so each sweep looks once (`CrmCaptureOutbox.later`: the next look, no attempt counted, no error, the lease dropped) — never a backoff, and nothing re-marks it from a page. (4) The CRM tells this app when a due settles (its REQ-127): `POST /payments/due-settled { dueId }` with `Authorization: Bearer <PPWK_SETTLED_TOKEN>` (constant-time; unset → hard-closed 403; no due → 400) makes the watch that names the due look NOW (`CrmLeadCapture.lookNow` by the outbox's `["crm-capture-due", dueId]` index, written and re-pointed by `addSettleWatch`, dropped with the watch) and answers `{ ok, looked }`; a due no watch names is acknowledged and nothing is looked at. (5) The fake's `POST /me/plan/fake-paid { quiet: true }` answers the record as STORED (a read would settle it), and the fake's `dueOpen` refuses a due it does not hold (`due-missing`, the real client's 404) instead of reading it as settled.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the rules are the coordinator's order of calls and one HTTP gate, exercised on the fakes · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-133 choose-plan — current() is the one read: … settled is active on that read, the tier and the paid notice follow by the sweep; open, it stays pending and the watch keeps looking"; every former `refresh` test now reads through `current`) · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-131 the page minted …" amended: a fixed cadence — the next look the next minute sweep's, no attempt, no error, no lease; "REQ-133 lookNow(dueId) — the CRM's settled notice: the watch on that due is looked at at once, the plan active before its minute; an unknown due is nothing") · `backend/src/users/domain/data/crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts` ("REQ-133 outbox — later() … watchByDue …; a newer pick's watch re-points the due index") · `backend/src/users/entrypoints/payments-controller/due-settled.int.test.ts` ("REQ-133 POST /payments/due-settled — closed without PPWK_SETTLED_TOKEN or with a wrong one; with it, the watch on the due is looked at now and the plan is active without any read of it") · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-131: paid on the page and the receipt tab closed …" amended: the backend is watched from the outside — the CRM's tier flips to Monster by the sweep before any read of the plan, and `activatedAt` precedes the first read; "REQ-056 …" no longer presses a refresh: settings reads the plan and the read finds the due settled).
**Evidence (2026-11-02):** RED first — 14 tests calling `flow.refresh` rewritten to `current` and failing (`a due paid while nobody presses anything`: the read did not settle), `lookNow is not a function`, `outbox.later is not a function`, the callback test's route 404, the cadence assertion red on the old backoff. One find on the way: `sign-in-landing` "REQ-091 … a paid pick still waiting on its pay page" went red because the FAKE read a due it did not hold as "not open" and the new read settled it — the fake now refuses an unknown due like the real client (404), and the read leaves the plan as stored. GREEN: `deno task test:unit` → `626 passed | 0 failed` + jest `679 passed`; `deno task test:int` → `327 passed | 0 failed`; `deno check` on `mod-root.ts`, the test files, `front-end/routes/plan/return.tsx`, `front-end/clients/profile.ts` clean; `deno lint` on the changed files: only the pre-existing `require-await` on `crossed`; e2e on the host (`shots run … --filter '/REQ-131|REQ-056/'`) → `✓ REQ-056 · 1.3s`, `✓ REQ-131 … · 118.2s` (two sweep minutes on a 60 s cadence — hence the 55 s), `2 pass · 0 fail`; the REQ-131 story again after the cadence change (`WATCH_EVERY_MS` 55 s): `✓ REQ-131 … · 57.4s` — one sweep minute.

## REQ-134 — A list of a user's records is read in batches, never one KV read per record
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-03, after 1,017 customers were loaded into Alex's account: "we need to paginate this information via the api cause customers take a long time to load now and its affecting other pages too."
**Found (prod, 2026-11-03, as Alex, 1,019 customers):** `GET /api/customers` 33 s, `/api/clients` 19 s, `/api/analytics/dashboard` 47 s, `/api/jobs` 46 s, `/api/quotes` 35 s, `/api/search?q=` 21 s, `/api/analytics/clients/top` 48 s. Every store's `listByUser` walks the user's index and then does ONE `kv.get` per record, awaited in turn — 1,019 round trips to Deno KV at ~30 ms each — and the dashboard, jobs, quotes and search coordinators each call it, so every page paid it.
**Requirement (read from that):** records behind an index are read in batches: `readMany(kv, keys)` in `@core/data/kv` reads with `kv.getMany` in chunks of ten (KV's limit) with the chunks in flight together (eight lanes), answering in key order with `null` for a missing key; `indexedIds(kv, prefix)` lists an index's values. Every `listByUser`/`listByInvoice`/`listByConversation` that fetched one record at a time (customers, quotes, invoices, payments ×2, payment terms, files, entries, accounts, conversations, messages, references) reads through it, with each store's own filter (deleted, owner) unchanged.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/core/data/kv/read-many.test.ts` ("REQ-134 readMany …": 25 keys are three getMany calls of ≤10, answered in key order, a missing key null, no keys no call; chunksOf) · integration `backend/src/crm/domain/data/customer-store/int.test.ts` ("REQ-134 customer-store — 250 customers listByUser: all 250, the deleted one left out, another user's never") · e2e n/a — a read-path change with no UI of its own; the prod timings above and below are the evidence.

## REQ-135 — The customers list is paged, searched and filtered by the API; the page draws one page
**Source:** the same ask (REQ-134): "we need to paginate this information via the api".
**Requirement (read from that):** `GET /clients?page=&pageSize=&q=&status=` answers ONE page: `{ items: CustomerCard[], page, pageSize, total, totalPages, counts, summary, loop }` — `pageSize` 25 by default and 100 at most, `page` clamped to the pages there are; `q` matches name, business, email, phone (digits), address or notes, case-insensitive; `status` one of the board's chips (`active|lead|owes|regular|cold`) or `all`; `counts` are the chip counts over what `q` matched; `summary` (`totalClients, activeJobs, owedCents, quietCount`) and `loop` (the three to call next: leads and owes, longest quiet first) are over the whole roster — the hero and the loop strip read them, never a page. Cards are sorted by name. The rules are pure (`analytics/domain/business/clients-page`). `GET /customers?page=&pageSize=&q=` answers the same envelope over plain `Customer` rows; without any of the three it answers the array it always has (the quotes picker, the assistant and the dashboard read it so). The /clients page fetches a page from the API on mount and again on every search, chip or page change (search debounced); the board draws the items it is handed and a pager (`Page x of y`, previous/next) — no list-wide filtering on the client any more.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/analytics/domain/business/clients-page/test.ts` ("REQ-135 clients-page — …": pageOf clamps and counts; matchesQuery on each field and phone digits; sortByName; countByStatus; summarize + loopPicks; clientsPage composes them) · integration `backend/src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/paging.int.test.ts` ("REQ-135 GET /clients — 30 customers: page 1 of 25, page 2 of 5, total 30; q narrows; status chips; counts and summary"), `backend/src/crm/entrypoints/customer-controller/paging.int.test.ts` ("REQ-135 GET /customers — the array without page; the envelope with it; q") · e2e `e2e/clients-pages/clients-pages.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-135: thirty customers — the page shows twenty-five, says Page 1 of 2, next shows five, a search shows one, the crumb counts thirty").

**RED first:** `read-many.test.ts` — `The requested module './mod.ts' does not provide an export named 'chunksOf'`; `clients-page/test.ts` — `Module not found …/clients-page/mod.ts`; both paging int tests — `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` (the array where the envelope must be). `customer-store/int.test.ts` was green before the change too — an in-memory KV hides the round trips — so it is the refactor's guard, and the unit test on a counting fake is the proof of batching (25 keys → getMany calls of 10, 10, 5). ## REQ-136 — a search-select component: type to filter, pick a result
**Source (Raphael, 2026-11-03):** "lets make a search compoenet. its a drop down that lets me type and filters results so i can select it. dont put it anywhere, just let me see it locally on a test page with 1000 rows for now."
**Requirement:** A reusable island, `SearchSelect`, is a text box with a drop-down: typing filters the options as you type (case- and accent-insensitive; a match at the start of the label ranks above a match at the start of a word, which ranks above a match anywhere), the arrow keys move a highlight, Enter or a click picks the highlighted option, Escape closes the list, and the picked option's label fills the box. Only the first 50 matches are rendered, with the count of the rest shown, so a thousand rows stay instant. It is mounted nowhere in the product; a dev-only test page, `/dev/search-select`, shows it over 1,000 generated rows and prints the pick under it. The page is a 404 on the real deploy (`DENO_DEPLOY` set).
**Tests:** unit — `front-end/lib/search-select.test.ts` (ranking, accents, the 50 cap, the wrap-around highlight); integration — n/a, no backend is touched; e2e — `e2e/search-select/search-select.e2e.test.ts` (the test page: 1,000 rows, typing narrows the list to matches only, the keyboard and the mouse both pick, the pick is printed).
**Evidence (2026-11-03):** RED — `lib/search-select.test.ts`: `Module not found` (type-check failed, 6 errors); the story: `the page never showed "1,000 rows"` (15.6 s timeout, the route did not exist). GREEN — `deno test -A lib/search-select.test.ts` → `5 passed | 0 failed`; `shots run e2e/search-select/search-select.e2e.test.ts` → `✓ REQ-136 … · 1.4s`, `1 pass · 0 fail`; `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on the six new files. Two of the story's own queries were wrong on first green and were corrected from the evidence frames: "mar" matches 250 rows (the cap holds, so nothing narrows below 50) → "row 99" (11 rows); "row 0" matches one row, so there is no second row to click → "row 10" (11 rows). The island itself needed one fix: a word-start match was found by the first occurrence only ("Omar Martinez" ranked as anywhere), now any ` q` occurrence ranks as a word start. Mounted nowhere; local only: `deno task serve` → http://localhost:5280/dev/search-select.
