## REQ-386 — The assistant keeps the customer details typed in the message: full name, "Bob wants …", a bare ZIP, the address on the customer line (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m17)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `m17` — "Assistant loses customer details from the message (names, zip, Bob not picked up, address)"; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `deb85b35` (fleet-6 line 218: "prefilled 'Gutierrez family' and 'Okafor' although I wrote 'Maria Gutierrez' and 'Daniel Okafor'", address empty though the text had zip 78745; fleet-9 line 98: "never asked which customer after 'Bob wants…'"; fleet-3 report #18: after a reload the thread shows "Customer: Dave Roof" without the job address).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** `shared/quote-flow/quick-quote-prefill.ts` `extractCustomerName` read a name only right after a "this is / for / para" lead-in, from the first match, stopping at punctuation — "for the Gutierrez family. Maria Gutierrez, …" → "Gutierrez family", "para Okafor (Daniel Okafor)" → "Okafor", "Bob wants 6 recessed lights" → null. `extractServiceAddress` needed a house number + street word, so "zip 78745" gave nothing. `backend/.../handle-chat-message/mod.ts` `customerFromTypedFacts` depends only on that extracted name / phone / email, so the existing Bob was never bound. `backend/.../handle-wizard-answer/mod.ts` wrote the customer transcript line as `{label}: {name}` only.
**Requirement:** (1) a full "First Last" name in the message that shares a word with a surname / household lead-in wins over it ("Maria Gutierrez", "Daniel Okafor"); an unrelated Capitalized pair never does. (2) With no lead-in, "<Name> wants / needs / asked / would like" (ES "quiere / necesita / pidió") names the customer; a pronoun or a lowercase word there never does. (3) A bare ZIP is kept as the job address — "Austin, TX 78745" with city/state, "zip 78745" / "código postal 78745" as the ZIP; a 5-digit number with neither is never a ZIP. (4) The chat path binds the one same-owner customer whose whole name is typed as Capitalized words (`findCustomerNamedInText` in `shared/quote-flow/customer-dedupe.ts`) when the extracted facts match nobody; two different customers named → nothing bound. (5) The wizard's customer transcript line (and the conversation preview) carries the job address the step settled on: "Customer: Dave Roof — 88 Oak Hollow Dr, Austin TX 78745" (`wizardAnswer.pick.transcriptAddress`, en + es).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/c2-customer-name-extract.test.ts` ("REQ-386 m17 …": Gutierrez family → Maria Gutierrez, para Okafor (Daniel Okafor) → Daniel Okafor, household-only and unrelated-pair guards, "Bob wants …" → Bob, pronoun / job-word guards, zip / código postal / City, ST ZIP, no-ZIP guards, `findCustomerNamedInText` whole-name / accent-blind / lowercase / partial / two-customer guards) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` ("REQ-386 m17: create_quote after 'Bob wants 6 recessed lights' binds the contractor's existing Bob", "… Maria Gutierrez, zip 78745' is bound") and `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts` ("REQ-386 m17 handle-wizard-answer: the customer transcript line carries the job address …", "… picking a customer with an address on file shows it …") · e2e n/a — every behaviour is a pure extractor (unit) or a coordinator the HTTP route calls directly (integration, real stores, stub LLM); the island reads the same pure functions, so a browser story would only re-render their output.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-customer-name-extract off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/c2-customer-name-extract.test.ts` → 9 failed (`Expected "Maria Gutierrez" Received "Gutierrez family"`, `Expected "Daniel Okafor" Received "Okafor"`, `Expected "Bob" Received null`, `Expected "78745" Received null`, `Expected "Austin, TX 78745" Received null`, `findCustomerNamedInText is not a function` ×3); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv …/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts …/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts --filter REQ-386` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed" (customerId `undefined`; "Customer: Dave Roof" without the address; "Customer: Maria Lopez" without the address). GREEN — the jest unit project "Test Suites: 209 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2014 passed"; `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/` → "ok | 111 passed | 0 failed"; `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/` → 487 passed, 1 failed — `openai/smk.test.ts` "REQ-368 … no allowlist keeps every tool", which fails identically on untouched deb85b35. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on the touched modules and the new test; `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched source file (the two int.test.ts files were already unformatted at baseline; only the added blocks are formatted).
## REQ-420 — A business address never repeats its state: a one-line street is split on save, and the one-line render skips what the street already ends with (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m28)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `m28` — "Business address repeats the state ('Austin, TX 78702, TX')" (fleet-4 stdout:223 "I entered "1200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702" and confirmed Texas"); RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** the /welcome address step (`front-end/islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx` ~587-665) is valid on a non-empty Street alone, and city/postal stay blank unless a Mapbox suggestion is picked (none on dev); the state comes from the earlier state step. So `PUT /profile/address` stored `{street: "1200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702", state: "TX"}` verbatim, and `composeAddressLine` (`backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/mod.ts`) appended ", TX" blindly → "1200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702, TX" on the public quote. Introduced by 69b4ed4f.
**Requirement:** (1) the address save path (`PUT /profile/address`) splits a whole one-line address typed into `street` — it has a comma and ends with a state (code or name) and/or ZIP — into street / city / state / ZIP with the onboarding chat's own parser (`extractAddressOnly`, hoisted to `backend/src/core/business/address-parse/mod.ts` and re-exported from the onboarding module); a value the client sent for city/state/postal wins, only empty ones are filled; a plain street ("123 Main St, Suite 200") is stored untouched. The parser also strips a spelled-out state ("Austin, Texas 78701" no longer reads "Texas" as the city). (2) `composeAddressLine` does not repeat a state, ZIP or city that a (legacy, unsplit) street already ends with. No WelcomeWizard change.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/core/business/address-parse/mod.test.ts` ("REQ-420 m28 …": the demo's exact input + TX → `{street: "1200 E Cesar Chavez St", city: "Austin", state: "TX", postal: "78702"}`; sent fields win; spelled-out state + ZIP+4; plain streets / street + unit / "Washington Ave, Suite 5" untouched; `extractAddressOnly` strips "Texas") and `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/compose-address-line.test.ts` ("REQ-420 m28 …": `{street: '1200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702', state: 'TX'}` → "1200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702"; "12 Texas Ave" / "5 Tx Rd" still get their city/state half) · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/business-address-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-420 (demo m28): PUT with a whole one-line address …": the app booted over HTTP, the wizard's exact body PUT → the response and a fresh GET carry the split fields) · e2e n/a — the wizard is unchanged; the integration test drives the real PUT with the exact body the wizard sends, and the public quote's addressLine is `composeAddressLine`, unit-pinned on the demo's row.

## REQ-371 — The customer's pointer and click wave land on what they pointed at, follow it on the stage, and a last touch fades (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m10)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issue `m10` — "Customer pointer/click ripple misplaced on stage (2 weeks vs 1 week, sticky hover, stale pointer)"; RCA analyst LIKELY (low confidence), skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** `front-end/islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx` `anchorOf` took `document.elementFromPoint` at pointerdown and handed it to `recorder.idOf`, which walks up to the nearest mirrored ancestor (`mirror-record.ts` `idOf`). The customer's own pill (`[data-demo-overlay]`) is never mirrored and takes pointer events, so a point under it named an ANCESTOR's box (or only the viewport fraction) — the stage's wave landed on another row. `front-end/islands/DemoStage.tsx` placed the click wave once at `placeOnStage(m.a)` and never again, so a replay whose layout moved after the click left the wave on the wrong row. A touch pointer gets no pointerleave, so the customer's last tap stayed drawn on the stage indefinitely and read as a sticky hover (pair 2 line 106). The "stale pointer on New customer after Esc" (pairs 4/10) was the customer's real resting mouse — not a bug.
**Requirement:** (1) the customer's pointer and clicks are anchored from the hit-test stack (`document.elementsFromPoint`), skipping every `[data-demo-overlay]` element, so the pill never steals the anchor (`anchorAt` in `front-end/lib/demo-mode/pointer-anchor.ts`); (2) the stage's click wave keeps its anchor and is placed again on every layout pass of the replay, like the pointer (`placeWavesAgain`); (3) a touch pointer (`pointerType === "touch"`) is let go — a `leave` is sent — TOUCH_REST_MS (3 s) after the last touch; a mouse or pen pointer is never faded (`createTouchFade`).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-customer-pointer.test.ts` ("REQ-371 (demo m10, cycle 2) …": `anchorAt` with the pill on top of the stack names the row under it with its in-box point, overlay-only stack → fraction only; `pageTopAt`; `placeWavesAgain` moves a wave whose node moved and keeps the array otherwise; `createTouchFade` timing for touch / mouse / pen / cancel; the overlay and the stage wired to them); the REQ-180/REQ-242 source pins in `demo-mode-motion.test.ts` and `demo-mode-mirror-wiring.test.ts` follow the anchoring into pointer-anchor.ts · integration n/a — no backend or wire change (the anchor shape is unchanged) · e2e n/a — the browser lane is not run in the demo-loop fix step, and the misplacement needs the pill over a mirrored row on a second live device; the hit-test-stack rule is pinned against a recorder double that walks up like mirror-record.ts.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-customer-pointer-anchor off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — with `pointer-anchor.ts` holding today's behaviour (topmost element), `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-mode-customer-pointer` → 10 failed, 1 passed; the anchor under the pill named `body` (id 1) instead of the "2 weeks" row (Expected 4 / Received 1), an overlay-only stack still named body, no touch fade, islands unwired. GREEN — the same file 11 passed; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 209 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2012 passed"; `deno test -A lib/` in front-end → "ok | 170 passed | 0 failed"; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on `islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx`, `islands/DemoStage.tsx`, `lib/demo-mode/pointer-anchor.ts`; `deno fmt` applied to those (both islands were fmt-clean at the base) and the touched tests.
## REQ-382 — Suggested prices fit the job: the basis line names only what the customer supplies, the model answers in dollars, and a gut / remodel has a plausibility floor (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M22)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `M22`: "Suggested prices far too low (regression)". A master-bath gut (slab drain move, heated floor, 60in double vanity, glass) whose client supplied only the faucets came back Competitive $1,850 / Market $2,250 / Premium $2,750; the contractor priced it at $28,000. RCA analyst LIKELY, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/suggest-prices/mod.ts` (1) REQ-332's `deriveBasis` correctly reads "(faucets supplied by client / grifos los pone la clienta)" as `labor_materials_as_noted`, but the basis line then said "price the labor and only the materials the contractor provides", which asked for a labor-only price on the whole gut; (2) the model wrote an integer `priceCents` (`prompts.suggestPrices`), where one dropped zero is a 10x error; (3) nothing compared the tiers with the size of the job: the only floor was a dollar amount the contractor typed (REQ-260); (4) the "Confirmed scope" sent beside the message was v1's 3 bullets (M20), and nothing told the model that a summary does not make the job smaller.
**Requirement:** (a) When the customer supplies items, the pricing request NAMES those items (`customerSuppliedItems`) and says to exclude only them and price everything else, labor and materials, in full. Only a blanket "labor only / materials not included" (`isLaborOnly`) asks for labor alone. (b) The model returns whole US dollars (`"price": <int>`), and the code converts to cents (a legacy `priceCents` answer is still read as cents). (c) A gut / remodel has a plausibility floor read off its trade and size (`price-floor/plausibilityFloorCents`: kitchen $12,000, bathroom $6,000, other room $3,000, plus $500 for each scope item past three, up to 15 items; halved for blanket labor-only; 0 for jobs that are not a gut or remodel). Tiers under the floor are re-asked once, naming the job size and the dollars unit. If they are still under it, they are lifted to the floor, keeping their spread and order (as REQ-260 does for stated costs). (d) The confirmed scope is labelled "a short summary of that message — it never makes the job smaller", and the full original message is always sent.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/price-basis/test.ts` ("REQ-382 M22 …": deriveBasis on the faucet text, customerSuppliedItems names only the faucet clause, isLaborOnly only for blanket wording) and `backend/src/agents/domain/business/price-floor/test.ts` ("REQ-382 M22 …": a master-bath gut floor ≥ $8,000 > the demo's $2,750, kitchen > bathroom > other > 0, small jobs 0, Spanish gut, labor-only halves, one supplied item does not) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/suggest-prices/int.test.ts` ("REQ-382 M22 …", SuggestPrices with the stub LLM: the supplied item is named and everything else is priced; the scope is labelled a summary and the full message is sent; dollars → cents and the prompt never asks for cents; the demo's $1,850 tiers are re-asked once naming the dollars unit and the gut; a model that stays low ships tiers ≥ $8,000, ascending) · e2e n/a: the numbers come from a live LLM that the browser lane stubs, so a browser story could only replay the stub. ## REQ-375 — After a quote is sent, the assistant makes a price change itself as the next Version; it never sends the contractor to a "Re-open" button that isn't there (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M11)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `M11` — "Assistant tells user to tap 'Re-open' on sent quote card; no such button exists" (related `B1`: revise_quote never offered to the model). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on deb85b35):** `prompts.systemTerms` (`lang/en.json` / `lang/es.json`) said unconditionally "Do NOT change line items or prices here… tell them to tap Re-open on the quote card above". A conversation stays in `currentPhase: "terms"` after the send (`AgentPhase = "quote" | "terms"`), so `SYSTEM_PROMPT_TERMS` keeps answering after the quote is sent. The know-my-price path never emits an action_card, so there was no card at all, and on an issued quote `ReopenQuote` refuses anyway (`QuoteAlreadySentError`). The same prompt then names `revise_quote`, but `chatToolsFor` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-routing/mod.ts`) never offered it in either phase (`ALL_TOOLS` lacked it; terms returned only change_order + update_job_details), so the model had no working path.
**Requirement:** (1) `revise_quote` is offered to the chat model in both phases (`ALL_TOOLS` and the terms list in `chatToolsFor`). (2) Every tool a chat prompt tells the model to call is one the phase actually offers (guard test over `TOOL_DEFS`). (3) The terms prompt depends on the bound quote's state (`systemPromptTermsFor` in `backend/src/agents/domain/business/llm-prompts/mod.ts`, picked by `HandleChatMessage`): an issued, unsigned quote → make the change with `revise_quote` (new work → `change_order`) and say it is saved as the next Version, ready to publish — never "tap Re-open"; a signed quote → `change_order` only; a locked, unsent quote that has a quote card in the thread → `revise_quote`, and Re-open on the card is mentioned as the way to edit by hand; anything else → `revise_quote`, no Re-open. ## REQ-407 — One "Payment received" per invoice card, no glyph chevron, a short scheduled date (demo-loop cycle 2, issues m30 + p13-f)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issues `m30` — "Two 'Payment received' buttons on one invoice card and a stray glyph after 'Adjust invoice'" — and `p13-f` — "'Scheduled to send 2026-11-26' next to 'Due Nov 19'" (fleet-3 stdout:44, :171). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** (1) `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` gives an out card the stage CTA `invoicesPage.cta.outReceived` ("Payment received", REQ-018) and the same back-foot row ALSO rendered `data-cy=invoice-payment-received` for `out | overdue` (introduced 3b445e28) — both call `doPaymentReceived`. (2) The "Adjust invoice" toggle appended a literal `▾` (U+25BE); REQ-366's guard only covered Dingbats U+2700–27BF, and the app's web fonts carry no Geometric Shapes, so headless Chromium drew a tofu box. (3) The scheduled subline passed `inv.scheduledFor` raw (ISO) while every other card date goes through the card's `fmtDate`.
**Requirement:** an out-for-payment card shows ONE "Payment received" (its stage CTA); the extra `invoice-payment-received` button stays only on an overdue card, whose CTA is "Nudge" (the detail panel's button is unchanged). "Adjust invoice" draws `<Icon name="chevron-down">`. A scheduled card reads "Scheduled to send Nov 26" / "Programada para enviar nov 26" — the same short date as the due dates. The card's date + secondary-action rules live in `front-end/lib/invoice-card.ts` (`cardDate`, `hasSecondaryPaymentReceived`, `scheduledSubline`). REQ-366's glyph guard now also bans U+25A0–25FF (Geometric Shapes), so the three other hits it found became icons too: FieldTasksPage's ◀ / ▶ day buttons (`chevron-left` / `chevron-right`) and PhoneChat's ▶ Play (`play`). The Arrows block (U+2190–21FF) is NOT banned: the app uses → / ← deliberately in 43 lang strings and 38 code lines (REQ-247's CTA arrow among them) and the demo saw them render; converting them is a separate change.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/invoice-card.test.ts` ("REQ-407 m30 …" / "REQ-407 p13-f …": out has no secondary Payment received, overdue keeps it; the scheduled subline is "Scheduled to send Nov 26" in en and the es short date, never ISO) and `front-end/lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx` (REQ-366 guard widened to U+25A0–25FF; chevron-down/left/right and play render as SVG paths) · integration n/a — front-end rendering only, no backend or wire change · e2e `e2e/invoice-card-c2/invoice-card-c2.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-407 (demo m30, p13-f) …": a real out card's back row has exactly one "Payment received", "Adjust invoice" holds `data-icon="chevron-down"` and no U+25A0–25FF char, a scheduled card's subline reads "Scheduled to send <Mon D>" with no ISO date).

## REQ-387 — A stated N-payment schedule ("30% deposit, 40% at cabinets install, 30% at completion") pre-fills the wizard's Custom payment option; the know-my-price path's raw job details say they will be tidied up (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M25)
**Source:** Raphael, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issue `M25` — "'I know my price' path uses raw message as job details, misreads 3-payment terms" (pair 7: "Payment: 'De tu mensaje: Depósito + saldo' ✗ — I wrote 30% deposit / 40% at cabinets / 30% completion (3 payments)"; "job details = my raw text"). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** `extractPaymentTerms` (`shared/quote-flow/quote-facts.ts`) knew only 30/30/40, 50/50, a half deposit, `N% … deposit` → `deposit_bal`, and net 15 — no N-installment case, so the 30/40/30 sentence matched the single-figure deposit rule and `wizardPrefillFor` offered "Deposit + balance" (billed 20/80 by `computePaymentSplit`). Job details: `startQuoteFromRaw` stores `description = raw.trim()` and the Job Details picker is deferred to the end of the wizard by design (`needsJobPolish` → `openJobPicker`), so until then the price screen's JOB DETAILS recap shows the raw message with no word that it will be rewritten.
**Requirement:** (1) A run of 2+ consecutive percentages in the job text that adds up to exactly 100, in a text that talks about payment, is the stated schedule: 30/30/40 and 50/50 map onto their presets; any other split is a custom schedule `{ kind: "custom", splits, milestones }` with each payment's own words ("deposit", "at cabinets install", "at completion"). It wins over the single-figure "N% deposit" rule; percentages that do not sum to 100, or carry no payment word, are not a schedule. (2) The payment step pre-selects the Custom option with it — value "30% deposit / 40% at cabinets install / 30% at completion" (or "30 / 40 / 30" when a payment has no words), which the one payment split bills 30/40/30 — and opening Custom starts on verify with those splits. (3) On the know-my-price path (no suggested pricing, no confirmed option), the price screen's JOB DETAILS recap adds "We'll tidy this up before you send." / "Lo dejaremos en limpio antes de enviarlo." (`asstChat.price.tidyNote`, en + es).

## REQ-370 — The stage never shows the customer's page unstyled: the frame appears once the replay's stylesheets are in (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m23)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `m23` — "Stage's first frame drew the sidebar unstyled for about a minute" (fleet-r561db6d4-1: first frame at 09:07:56 unstyled, "styled correctly by the next look"). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** `shared/demo-mode/stage-frame.ts` `stageFrameLook` returned `visibility:"visible"` on `mirrored` alone, and `front-end/islands/DemoStage.tsx` `take()` set `mirrored` the moment a snapshot was applied. The snapshot rebuilds the customer's `<link rel=stylesheet href=/…css?__frsh_c=…>` in a fresh srcdoc document; the staff browser fetches each sheet for the first time, and until it lands the page lays out with the UA defaults (blue links, white boxes, focus outline). REQ-305's `Replayer.styled()` knew this but only gated pointer anchoring, never the frame's visibility.
**Requirement:** the stage shows the mirror frame only once the replay is styled (`Replayer.styled()`) — or `STYLE_WAIT_MS` (1.5 s) after the demo's first snapshot, so a sheet that never answers cannot hold the stage dark. Until then "Connecting to {name}…" stays up and the pill does not say Live (REQ-309: the pill and the overlay key on the same fact, the frame being shown). `stageFrameLook` takes a `styled` flag (`frameReady({ styled, waited })`); the stage re-checks it on every applied snapshot, on every replay layout pass (a stylesheet's load fires one) and on the fallback timer; a new demo starts unstyled again.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-stage-styled-reveal.test.ts` ("REQ-370 …": `stageFrameLook` mirrored && !styled → hidden, no waiting overlay; `frameReady` waits for the sheets at most STYLE_WAIT_MS; the island feeds `styled`, derives it from `rep.styled()` through `frameReady`, has the STYLE_WAIT_MS fallback timer, re-checks in `replace()` and `take()`, keys the connecting overlay and the Live label on `look.visibility`); REQ-297's `jest/unit/demo-stage-waiting.test.ts` and REQ-309's `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror-wiring.test.ts` follow the new flag/label · integration (module level, in the same jest file — the real recorder → JSON wire → real replayer → `frameReady` → `stageFrameLook`: a snapshot whose sheet has not loaded is hidden, its load event reveals it; a sheet that never answers is revealed at STYLE_WAIT_MS; the jest `integration` project is HTTP-against-the-stack and this has no server part) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-242's story, new step before 2: the staff browser's frame stylesheets are held by `page.route`; once the snapshot is in the frame and its sheet is asked for, the frame is not visible and "Connecting to…" is; then released).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local Mac host, branch fix/c2-stage-styled-reveal off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-stage-styled-reveal` → "Tests: 8 failed, 1 passed, 9 total" (`Expected: "hidden" Received: "visible"`; `stageFrame.frameReady is not a function`; the island's wiring patterns absent); `SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` with the island + stage-frame reverted → "✗ … expectation failed: REQ-370 (m23): the frame is not shown while its stylesheets load — expected false, got true" (2.9 s — the bug, in Chromium). GREEN — the jest file "Tests: 9 passed, 9 total"; `--testPathPattern demo-` 18 suites / 236 passed; the whole unit project "Test Suites: 209 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2010 passed"; `front-end/lib/stage-a11y.test.tsx` 2 passed; `deno lint`, `deno check`, `deno fmt --check` clean on the touched files; the same shots story passes the REQ-370 step and steps 2–10 and stops at step 11 ("End from the customer": `[data-cy='demo-pill']` never hides, 15 s) — the host's known demo-end race REQ-293 recorded on untouched demo-fixes at the same line.

## REQ-414 — /login and /verify carry an EN | ES switch that persists pm_lang; the Spanish-first default stays (demo-loop cycle 2, issue p4)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issue `p4` — "Landing and /login open in Spanish for an English browser; /login has no language switch" (RCA analyst FEATURE_GAP, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** the Spanish default is deliberate — `pickLangFromAcceptLanguage` (`front-end/lib/lang.ts`) ignores the header and returns "es" (09047711, product decision), and stays. The gap: `front-end/routes/login.tsx` rendered brand, heading, subtitle, `<LoginForm/>` and `<SiteFooter/>` with no EN/ES control, and resolved its language from the pm_lang cookie only (ignoring `?lang=`), so a visitor who landed on /login directly could not switch. `/verify` had the same cookie-only resolve and no control — and ignored the `&lang=` /login's form already hands it. Neither recorded its language on `ctx.state.lang`, so with no cookie `<html lang>` followed the browser ("en") while the page painted Spanish.
**Requirement:** /login and /verify mount the EN | ES toggle (`islands/PublicLangToggle.tsx`, `data-public-lang` links to the same page with `?lang=` set, `langToggleHref`), resolve their language through the public pages' ONE resolver (`front-end/lib/page-lang.ts` `resolvePageLang`: `?lang=` → pm_lang → Spanish), record it on `ctx.state.lang` (so `<html lang>` and the islands match the page), and persist an explicit `?lang=` pick to the pm_lang cookie (`pickedLangHeaders`, now shared with `lib/public-page.ts`); a tap on the toggle also persists client-side. With no choice both stay Spanish-first, whatever the browser's Accept-Language.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/login-lang-toggle.test.ts` ("REQ-414 …": both routes import/mount `PublicLangToggle` with `langToggleHref(…, "en"|"es")` and link `/public-lang.css`, resolve via `resolvePageLang(ctx.req)` + `ctx.state.lang = lang` with no cookie-only `langFromCookie(`, persist via `pickedLangHeaders(picked)`; the shared writer; the resolver's /login and /verify outcomes) · integration `jest/integration/login-lang-toggle.int.test.ts` ("REQ-414 …", over HTTP: an English browser with no choice gets Spanish + `<html lang="es">` + the EN link `/login?lang=en` and no cookie; `/login?lang=en` paints "Welcome back" and the island's "Text me a code", `<html lang="en">`, `set-cookie: pm_lang=en`; a pm_lang=en cookie opens English; /verify carries the toggle with the phone kept in its links, and `?lang=en` beats a pm_lang=es cookie and persists) · e2e `e2e/login-lang/login-lang.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-414: /login has an EN | ES toggle that flips the screen to English, remembers it, and flips back").
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-login-lang-toggle off demo-fixes deb85b35; stack `PORT=38417 deno task serve`):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --verbose unit/login-lang-toggle.test.ts` → "Tests: 6 failed, 1 passed, 7 total"; `FRONTEND_BASE_URL=http://localhost:38417 npx jest --selectProjects integration --verbose integration/login-lang-toggle.int.test.ts` → "Tests: 5 failed, 5 total" (no toggle: `Expected: true / Received: undefined`; `/login?lang=en` painted Spanish under `<html lang="en">`); `BASE_URL=… SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/login-lang -- --no-check` → "✗ REQ-414 … locator.getAttribute: Timeout 15000ms exceeded" (no toggle). ## REQ-381 — The help-me-price confirm strip submits what it shows: the contractor's own words, never the pre-selected version 1 (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M20)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issue `M20` — "'Looks right — confirm these details' uses version 1 instead of user text and skips Continue" (fleet-6 09:09:34: JOB DETAILS showed v1's 3 bullets after clicking the strip; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** the green strip (`data-cy="confirm-details"`, `front-end/islands/AsstChat.tsx`) echoes `pendingJobDetailsRaw` — the typed message — but its `onClick` was `applyJobOption`, the same handler as Continue. `applyJobOption` reads `jobOptions.find(o => o.id === selectedOptionId)`, and `settleJobOptions` pre-selects `drafts[0]` (v1); in confirm mode it stashes that card on `confirmedOptionRef`, overwrites `pendingJobDetailsRaw` with v1's bullets and opens price capture. So the strip looked like "confirm my text" but submitted v1 and advanced. Introduced by c3847643 (confirm-details step).
**Requirement:** clicking the strip confirms the contractor's own words: an option built from the typed message by the shared scope pass (`ownWordsOption` in `shared/quote-flow/own-words-option.ts` over `scopeBulletsFromRaw` — intent opener, price clause and pricing question stripped, one bullet per line; the typed lines as written when nothing scope-like survives) and advances to pricing with it (`confirmOwnWords` → `applyOption`). It never reads the selected card. The strip's label says what it submits — "Use what I wrote — continue" / "Usar lo que escribí — continuar" (`asstChat.confirmDetails.cta`). Continue still confirms the selected card.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/confirm-strip-own-words.test.ts` ("REQ-381 …": `ownWordsOption` → scope lines EN/ES, typed lines kept when degraded, null when empty; the strip's onClick is `confirmOwnWords`, which builds from `pendingJobDetailsRaw` and never reads `selectedOptionId`; the label in both languages names what it submits) · integration n/a — no backend or wire change; the pricing request already carries `scope`, the fix only changes which option the island confirms · e2e `e2e/confirm-strip-own-words/confirm-strip-own-words.e2e.test.ts` (options endpoint answers three "Version N" cards: clicking the strip lands on pricing with the typed scope in JOB DETAILS and in the prices request's `scope`, no v1 bullets, label "what I wrote"; Continue still confirms the first card).

## REQ-394 — A job name mid-sentence is lower case, and /quotes titles follow the app language (demo-loop cycle 2, issue p9)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `p9` — "Titles in Title Case or wrong language (quote titles, 'What should X cost?')"; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** (1) `shared/quote-flow/quote-price-guard.ts` `priceProblemItem` returned the raw line description, capital and all, into `chatCoordinator.priceMissing` — "What should Recessed lighting installation (6 lights) cost?". (2) `shared/quote-flow/agreement-title.ts` built `Acuerdo de ${job} de ${customer}` with the job's capital — "Acuerdo de Corte de césped semanal de Ana López". (3) `front-end/islands/QuotesPage.tsx` titled every card and the open panel with the stored primary `jobName`, so a quote made in English stayed English in the Spanish app although `jobNameByLang.es` existed. (4) English job names are stored in Title Case by design (REQ-276/REQ-337).
**Requirement:** one casing rule. An English job name is a LABEL and keeps its Title Case where it stands alone (thread-list row, quote card heading, "Godzilla's Concrete Patio Agreement"); wherever a job name or line description lands MID-SENTENCE it goes through `jobNameInSentence` (`shared/quote-flow/job-name.ts`): a sentence-case phrase loses its leading capital, a Title Case label is lowered word by word, acronyms (LED, HVAC) and mixed-case words (McDonald, iPhone) keep their case, and a "— <customer>" tail is left as written. Applied to the price ask's `{item}` (both languages) and the Spanish agreement title ("Acuerdo de corte de césped semanal de Ana López"). /quotes cards and the open panel title a quote with `quoteJobTitle(q, lang)` — `jobNameByLang[lang]` → `jobName` → `summaryByLang[lang]` → `summary` — and the panel's summary line reads `summaryByLang[lang]` first.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/title-casing.test.ts` ("REQ-394 …": `jobNameInSentence` sentence-case / Title Case / acronym / mixed-case cases; `priceProblemItem` lowers the line and the summary fallback; `agreementTitle` es lowers the job, keeps an acronym, en unchanged; `quoteJobTitle` picks the current language's name and falls back; QuotesPage imports and uses `quoteJobTitle` for cards and panel) and `jest/unit/ux-page-copy.test.ts` (REQ-036's ES title now "Acuerdo de concrete patio de Godzilla") · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` ("REQ-394 p9 handle-chat-message integration: the price ask lower-cases the line it names mid-sentence" — the demo's exact "$abc" turn → "What should recessed lighting installation (6 lights) cost?"; REQ-302's two price-ask tests now expect "panel swap") · e2e n/a — every change is a pure string rule pinned by unit tests against the real dictionaries plus the coordinator integration test; the /quotes wiring is one call to the pure `quoteJobTitle`, pinned on the island's source.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-title-casing off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit -- unit/title-casing` → "Tests: 11 failed, 3 passed" (`jobNameInSentence is not a function`; `Received: "Recessed lighting installation (6 lights)"`; `Received: "Acuerdo de Corte de césped semanal de Ana López"`; `quoteJobTitle is not a function`); `deno test -A --unstable-kv …/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts --filter "/REQ-302|REQ-394/"` → "FAILED | 1 passed | 3 failed". GREEN — `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Tests: 1 skipped, 2015 passed"; `deno test -A --unstable-kv` over handle-chat-message, send-quote, lock-quote, quote-store, render-quote-pdf, build-quote-cards → "ok | 141 passed | 0 failed"; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on QuotesPage.tsx, quote-doc.tsx, the three shared modules and the touched backend coordinators; `deno fmt` on every touched file (all clean at HEAD).
**Not in scope (left as is):** other `{job}` slots that sit mid-sentence ("Here's what I'd charge for {job}:", accepted-alert / inquiry / change-order lines) still receive the label as stored; chat-created quotes (create_quote in handle-chat-message) still store no `jobNameByLang`, so their /quotes title has no Spanish form to show.
## REQ-385 — A thread's labels agree everywhere: no "Drafting" chip on a question, one title rule (job, then "· customer"), "Picking job details" while the picker is re-opened, the customer card's unsent quote reads "Not sent" (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m6)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issue `m6` — "Status labels and headers disagree (Redactando vs header, LISTA PARA ENVIAR vs BORRADOR, header churn)"; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** (1) `threadChip` (`shared/quote-flow/chat-header.ts`) mapped status `none` — any thread with no quote, even a plain question — to `asstThreads.chip.drafting` ("Redactando") while the header for the same thread read "Nueva conversación" with no quote status. (2) `deriveChatHeader`'s title was `customerName || quote.jobName || newConversation`, so it swapped New conversation → job name → customer name as each was learned (the list's `threadTitle` already said "job · customer"; the SSR route used yet another rule, `conversation.customerName ?? title`). (3) The /customers card names a quote by `quote.status`, which stays `draft` until a real send (NW-10), so "BORRADOR" sat beside the assistant's "LISTA PARA ENVIAR". (4) `ListConversations.flowOf` (`backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/list-conversations/mod.ts`) and the chat derived `detailsPending` from `draft.polishRaw` only; the review card's pencil re-opens the job picker (`jobOptionsOpen`, `pickerMode: "polish"`) with no `polishRaw`, so "Ready to send" showed while the details were being rewritten.
**Requirement:** (1) A thread with no quote has no list chip (`threadChip` → `null`; AsstThreads renders none); the bill chip still rides on top. (2) The thread's title is one rule everywhere — `threadName` in `shared/quote-flow/thread-title.ts`: the job name, then "· customer" appended (customer alone when there is no job) — used by `deriveChatHeader`, the list's `threadTitle` and the SSR header of `/assistant/[threadId]`. (3) The customer card's unsent document state reads "Not sent" / "Sin enviar" (`clientsBoard.docState.draft`), never "Draft"/"Borrador" beside "Ready to send" — the lifecycle stays stamped on a successful send only (NW-10). (4) `draftOwesDetails` (chat-header.ts) is the one "job-details pick owed" rule: `polishRaw`, or the job picker open in "polish" mode (not the pre-quote "confirm" picker); the server list, the SSR header and AsstChat's header all read it.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/chat-header.test.ts` ("REQ-385 (cycle 2, m6) …": no chip for `none`; title grows job → "job · customer" and equals `threadTitle`; SSR route uses the derived `clientName`; `draftOwesDetails` polish/confirm/closed; AsstChat's header passes the open picker; en "Not sent" / es "Sin enviar"), with REQ-245/REQ-369 expectations updated in `jest/unit/chat-header.test.ts`, `thread-status.test.ts`, `failed-send-truth.test.ts`, `quote-lock.test.ts` · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/list-conversations/int.test.ts` ("REQ-385 (cycle 2, m6) the job-details picker re-opened …": wizard done → readyToSend; draft parks the open polish picker → list and header both "pickingDetails"; closed → readyToSend); `send-quote/chat-header.int.test.ts` title now "Roof · Ana Ruiz" · e2e `backend/src/agents/entrypoints/conversations-controller/thread-status.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-369's HTTP walk gains the re-opened-picker step over `POST /agents/conversations/:id/draft` → `GET /agents/conversations` row and header "pickingDetails"); the browser lane is not run in the demo-loop fix step.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-thread-status-labels off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern unit/chat-header` → "Tests: 7 failed, 26 passed" (all seven REQ-385 cases: chip `{kind:"draft",key:"asstThreads.chip.drafting"}` not null; title "Ana Ruiz" not "Fence install · Ana Ruiz"; `draftOwesDetails({jobOptionsOpen:true,pickerMode:"polish"})` false; docState.draft "Draft"); `deno test … list-conversations/int.test.ts conversations-controller/thread-status.e2e.test.ts` → "FAILED | 3 passed | 2 failed" (`header: "readyToSend", list: "readyToSend"` vs expected "pickingDetails"). ## REQ-373 — The customer's demo pill names the guide once: first name on the compact pill, no chip echoing the sentence, the details button labelled by the status (demo-loop cycle 2, issues m2 + p13-h)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issues `m2` — "Collapsed pill says only 'Connected'; expanded repeats the guide name; reopens expanded after reload" — and `p13-h` — "Pill text read three times by a screen reader"; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.

One pure helper, `pillCopy` (`shared/demo-mode/pill-copy.ts`); new keys `demoMode.statusShowDetails` / `demoMode.statusHideDetails` in en and es.

## REQ-427 — The onboarding Back button survives a reload: the wizard navigates the whole onboarding and opens at the first open step (demo-loop cycle 2, issue p13-s)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `p13-s` — "Onboarding Back button disappears after a reload"; RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** `front-end/islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx` built the visit's step list from the unanswered questions alone (`steps = openSteps(registry, snapshot)`, REQ-121) and started its index at 0 (or `indexAfterPlan`, an index into that short list). After a reload the steps answered before it were not in the list, so the current step was index 0, `canGoBack: index > 0` was false and `StepFooter` drew an empty `<span>` where Back goes.
**Requirement:** the wizard's index is a place in the WHOLE registry. It opens at the first open step — or, back from a plan pick, the first open step after the plan's slot (REQ-059) — `startIndex` in `front-end/lib/welcome-steps.ts`. Back goes to the step before, answered or not, prefilled from the snapshot, so it is there after any reload whenever a step precedes the current one. Continue / Skip (`nextIndex`) retrace the steps Back walked through, up to the furthest this visit reached; past that they stop only on the steps that were open when the wizard opened (REQ-121 unchanged going forward). The counter is the step's place in the onboarding (`stepCounter(registry, index)`): a new account and the plan pick's reload read exactly as before ("Step 5 of 10" on the state, REQ-253); a later login with only the business name and the logo open now reads Step 2, 8, 10 of 10 (was 8, 9, 10) — the business name IS the second step, and Back from it to the name reads Step 1.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/welcome-steps.test.ts` ("REQ-427 Back survives a reload: …", 3: the plan pick's reload opens at the state with Back through plan/email/business name/name and Continue retracing to the state; a later login opens at the business name with Back to the name, Continue never landing on an answered step it was not walked back through; the wizard bound to `registry[index]`, `nextIndex(registry, open, i, reached.current)`, `canGoBack: index > 0`; REQ-121's binding test and REQ-253's four counter tests amended to the registry index) · integration: n/a — no backend or wire change; the wizard's navigation is a pure rule over the snapshot it already receives · e2e `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-427: Back survives a reload — …": name and business name answered in the wizard, the page reloaded on the email, Back is there and walks to the business name and the name, each filled in, Continue walks forward to the email again; REQ-121's story amended to Step 2 / 8 / 10 of 10).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local, branch fix/c2-wizard-back-reload off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern welcome-steps` on the untouched lib + wizard → "Tests: 8 failed, 5 passed" (`startIndex is not a function`; the wizard not bound to the registry); `shots run e2e/onboarding-until-answered -- --no-check` with the baseline wizard + lib → "4 pass · 2 fail": REQ-427 "locator.waitFor: Timeout 15000ms exceeded" waiting for Back after the reload, REQ-121 "the page never showed "Step 2 of 10"". GREEN — the same jest file 13 passed; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 208 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2004 passed"; the same shots run "6 pass · 0 fail"; `shots run e2e/free-signup e2e/plan-picker e2e/wizard-enter e2e/onboarding-comms-lang -- --no-check` → "20 pass · 0 fail"; `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on `islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx` and `lib/welcome-steps.ts` (both already fmt-unclean at baseline, left as they were).
### REQ-253 AMENDMENT — by REQ-427: the counter is the step's place in the whole registry (`stepCounter(registry, index)`); the new-account and after-plan counts are unchanged, a later login with gaps reads each open step's own place (business name Step 2, logo Step 8, closing Step 10 of 10). Tests: `jest/unit/welcome-steps.test.ts`, `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts`.
### REQ-121 AMENDMENT — by REQ-427: the visit's open steps are the forward stops, no longer the whole navigation; Back reaches an answered question, and Continue retraces only what Back walked through. Tests: `jest/unit/welcome-steps.test.ts`, `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts`.
## REQ-374 — The demo pointer is always clearly visible and its name tag stays readable, off the content (demo-loop cycle 2, issues m9 + p8)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4), issues `m9` ("Presenter name tag invisible (opacity 0) most of the time, covers text when shown") and `p8` ("Pointer faint/hard to see and styled differently per side"); RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** REQ-242's design. `front-end/components/demo-mode/DemoPointer.tsx` set the tag's opacity to 0 `TAG_IDLE_MS` (1.5 s, `shared/demo-mode/motion.ts`) after the last x/y change, so every resting pointer had an invisible tag; while shown, `tagPlacement` put it right of and below the tip — on the content pointed at. The arrow's svg dropped to opacity .45 after `ARROW_IDLE_MS` (6 s) and to .55 when `outside`, with only a 1.6 px white stroke, so it read as a faint white arrow on light cards. The customer's colour (`CUSTOMER_COLOR`) was named nowhere on the stage.
**Requirement:** (1) The arrow is always fully opaque (`pointerLook().arrow === 1`; `ARROW_IDLE_MS` is gone), drawn with a dark outline over a wide white halo (plus a soft drop shadow) so it reads on light and dark content; `outside` is marked by the dashed ring alone. (2) The name tag sits above-left of the tip, away from the arrow's body and the content, flipping right / down only at the box's left / top edge (`tagPlacement`); at rest it fades to `TAG_REST_OPACITY` (0.6), never 0, and any re-placement (a new pointer object — move, re-anchor after a scroll — or an `outside` toggle) shows it fully again. The tag is `aria-hidden` (the pill names the presenters). (3) The stage pill names the customer's pointer colour with a `CUSTOMER_COLOR` dot (`data-cy="demo-customer-dot"`) by "Presenting to {name}"; presenter chips already carry each presenter's dot and "(you)".
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-pointer-look.test.ts` ("REQ-374 (demo m9/p8, cycle 2) …": above-left placement and its edge flips; `pointerLook` / `TAG_REST_OPACITY` (≥ .5, < 1) and no `ARROW_IDLE_MS`; DemoPointer's rest effect keyed on `[pointer, outside]`, no .45/.55; the stage pill's customer dot) and `front-end/lib/demo-pointer-look.test.tsx` (DemoPointer rendered for real (SSR): arrow svg opacity 1 inside and outside, a white halo path ≥ 3 wide under a colour-filled path with a dark outline, dashed ring only when outside; the tag is aria-hidden, placed by `right:`/`bottom:`, fully shown); REQ-242's `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror.test.ts` and `demo-mode-mirror-wiring.test.ts` updated to the new placement and rest look · integration n/a — no backend or wire change; the pointer's look is client-only rendering · e2e n/a — the browser lane is not run in the demo-loop fix step; the rendered markup is asserted by the SSR test and the rest/placement rules are pure functions.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local, branch fix/c2-demo-pointer-look off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-mode-pointer-look` → "Tests: 5 failed, 5 total" (placement `{left:false,up:false}` vs `{left:true,up:true}`; `pointerLook` undefined; `Expected pattern: /pointerLook\(/`; no `demo-customer-dot`); `deno test -A lib/demo-pointer-look.test.tsx` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed" (no white halo path; outside arrow opacity `0.55` vs `1`; tag aria-hidden `null` vs `"true"`). GREEN — the jest file 5 passed; `deno test -A lib/demo-pointer-look.test.tsx lib/stage-a11y.test.tsx` → "ok | 5 passed | 0 failed"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-` → "Test Suites: 209 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2006 passed"; `deno check` (DemoPointer, PeerPointer, DemoStage, DemoModeOverlay, motion.ts) exit 0; `deno lint` + `deno fmt` clean on every touched file.
## REQ-422 — One EN/ES click holds on the first dashboard visit: a profile read in flight cannot undo it (demo-loop cycle 2, issue m48)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `m48` — "First EN click on the first dashboard visit is ignored (two PUT /api/me)" (fleet-2 stdout:59); RCA analyst LIKELY / skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** the topbar EN button (`front-end/islands/DashTopbar.tsx`) calls `setLang("en")` and then a best-effort `PUT /api/me`. The authed islands call `refreshDash()` on mount (`DashSidebar.tsx:174`, `DashboardPage`, `AsstChat`), which reads `/profile` and the slow `/analytics/dashboard` together (`front-end/lib/dash-cache.ts` `refreshDash`). `writeCached` applied `setLang(snap.profile.user.language)` on every refresh, so a read started before the click and landing after it put the old "es" back — the first click looked ignored and a second click (a second PUT) was needed.
**Requirement:** a language the contractor picks locally (topbar toggle, Settings, wizard…) wins over any profile read that was already in flight when they picked it. `setLang` counts local choices (`langChoiceMark()` in `front-end/lib/i18n.ts`; the cache's server seed passes `{ fromServer: true }` and does not count); `refreshDash` notes the mark when its read starts and `writeCached` seeds the server's `user.language` only if no local choice happened since — otherwise the snapshot it caches carries the local choice instead. A read that starts after the choice still seeds the server's language as before. The topbar toggle also patches the cached profile's language at once (`patchCachedLanguage`), before the PUT lands.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/dash-cache.test.ts` ("REQ-422 (m48): …" ×3: a stale refresh started before the EN click does not revert the language and caches "en"; a refresh started after the choice still seeds the server's language; `patchCachedLanguage` updates the cached profile and its sessionStorage copy) · integration n/a — no backend or wire change; the race is purely client-side ordering of a read and a local choice, pinned with stub fetchers in the unit test · e2e `e2e/dash-lang-race/dash-lang-race.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-422 (demo m48): …": a Spanish account on /customers, the `/api/analytics/dashboard` read held open in the browser, one EN click, the read released → `<html lang>` stays "en", EN stays pressed, exactly one `PUT /api/me`, the server's profile says "en").
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-dash-lang-race off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/dash-cache.test.ts` → "FAILED | 11 passed | 2 failed" ("AssertionError: Values are not equal: the stale read flipped EN back to ES"; `patchCachedLanguage` not implemented); `shots run e2e/dash-lang-race -- --no-check` with the three source files at deb85b35 → "✗ … expectation failed: still EN after the stale read — expected "en", got "es"". GREEN — the same unit file "ok | 13 passed | 0 failed"; `deno test -A lib/` → "ok | 173 passed | 0 failed"; the same shots story "✓ REQ-422 … 10.2s"; REQ-367's `e2e/live-lang-switch` (topbar EN/ES) "✓ ×2"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` on the language/topbar/dash suites → "Test Suites: 208 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2001 passed"; `deno lint`, `deno check`, `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched file.
## REQ-419 — The customer card's back shows every row, is hidden from assistive tech while closed, and a single page has no "Page 1 of 1" (demo-loop cycle 2, issues m40, S7c, p13-k)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issues `m40` ("Back of the customer card clips its rows (ADDRESS, DOCUMENTS)"), `S7c` ("Pair 7 customer read a card's hidden back side as visible") and `p13-k` ("'Page 1 of 1' floating next to one card"); RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD for all three at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on demo-fixes deb85b35):** (m40) `.ccard2__panel` is `position:absolute; inset:0` inside `.ccard2 { overflow:hidden }` (`front-end/static/clients.css`), so the back is exactly the front's height; it is a flex column whose `.ccard2__panel-rows` groups carry `overflow:hidden` (so `min-height:0`) and shrink. Since REQ-145 (subscriptions) and REQ-323 (documents) added two more groups, the contact group lost its ADDRESS row and DOCUMENTS was half hidden. (S7c) the closed back (`islands/ClientsBoard.tsx`) was hidden by `opacity:0; pointer-events:none` only — no `aria-hidden`, `inert` or `visibility:hidden` — so screen readers and accessibility snapshots read it and its tel:/mailto: links took focus. (p13-k) REQ-135's pager rendered on `!rosterEmpty` with no `totalPages > 1` check, inside the `.ccards2` grid, so it took the grid cell beside a lone card.
**Requirement:** (1) the card's back scrolls as one (`.ccard2__panel { overflow-y:auto }`) and its head and row groups never shrink (`flex-shrink:0`), so every row (ADDRESS, SUBSCRIPTIONS, DOCUMENTS) is fully shown or scrolled to. (2) A closed back is `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert`, and `visibility:hidden` once its fade-out ends; the open back is exposed and focusable. (3) The pager renders only when there is more than one page, and sits under the cards grid (`.clay2__main` wraps grid + pager), never in a card's cell.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/clients-board-layout.test.tsx` ("REQ-419 …": ClientsBoard rendered via SSR — the closed panel is aria-hidden + inert; one page → no `.cpager`; two pages → the pager shows "Page 1 of 2" and is not a child of `.ccards2`; clients.css pins `overflow-y:auto` + `visibility:hidden` on the panel, `visibility:visible` when open, `flex-shrink:0` on the head and the row groups) · integration n/a — front-end markup and CSS only; no server or wire change · e2e `e2e/clients-pages/clients-pages.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-419 (demo-loop cycle 2: m40, S7c, p13-k) …": one customer with phone, email and address → no pager and no "Page 1 of 1"; the closed back is aria-hidden, inert and absent from the aria snapshot; opened → exposed, every row group's scrollHeight ≤ clientHeight, the DOCUMENTS group scrolls fully inside the panel, the address is visible), and REQ-135's story now expects no pager (not "Page 1 of 1") for a one-result search.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local, branch fix/c2-clients-board-layout off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/clients-board-layout.test.tsx` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed" (`aria-hidden` `- null + "true"`; "no 'Page 1 of 1'" `- Element {} + null`; "the pager is not a child of the cards grid"; "the panel scrolls: overflow-y:auto"); `shots run e2e/clients-pages -- --no-check` → "✗ REQ-419 … expectation failed: the page shows "Page 1 of 1" and should not". With the pager fix in and the S7c / m40 fixes reverted one at a time, the story fails at "the closed back is aria-hidden" and at "the contact group shows all its rows: {"cy":"contact","client":139,"scroll":153}" (the clipped ADDRESS row). GREEN — the unit file "ok | 4 passed"; `shots run e2e/clients-pages -- --no-check` → REQ-135, REQ-274, REQ-277, REQ-279, REQ-419 all ✓ ("5 pass · 0 fail"); `deno test -A lib/` → "ok | 174 passed | 0 failed"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 208 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 2001 passed"; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on `islands/ClientsBoard.tsx`, `islands/ClientsPage.tsx` and the new test; `deno fmt --check` clean on the new test (`ClientsBoard.tsx`, `clients.css` and the e2e file were already fmt-unclean at the base and were not reformatted).
## REQ-428 — The demo harness numbers a pair one way everywhere, and an agent cut off by the timeout still leaves its report, trace and stderr (demo-loop cycle 2, issues nc-pair-numbering + nc-pair6-report)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issues `nc-pair-numbering` — "Status line says [pair n] while persona inside is PAIR n+1" — and `nc-pair6-report` — "Pair 6 customer report missing; '(no report file — final message:)' empty"; RCA analyst + skeptic CONFIRMED/UPHELD at demo-fixes `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** `demo20b.sh` (the per-VM job, until now only in the host's `v2/demo-loop/`) printed `[pair $IDX]` with the 0-based VM index from the hostname in its status lines while every header said `PAIR $N` (`N=IDX+1`), so fleet-1 opened "[pair 1]" over Jorge's PAIR 2. Pair 6's customer agent ran into `timeout 1270` ("agents done at 1309s" = 21 + 20 + 1270) before writing `customer-report.md`; `claude -p` in text mode prints only on a clean exit, so `customer.out` was empty, and only `tail -2` of stderr (the token-rotator line) was kept — nothing of what it did survived.
**Requirement:** (1) one pair number everywhere: status lines read `[vm IDX · pair N]`, the same N as the `PAIR N` headers. (2) Agents run with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, so `<who>.out` is the live transcript; the fallback prints the run's final message (the `result` event), or — when there is none — the last 40 text/tool events, never raw JSON. (3) Each agent gets SIGTERM `DEMO_KILL_GRACE` (60 s) before its hard deadline and SIGKILL at it (`timeout -k`); its exit code is kept and a 124/137 prints "(<who> agent killed by timeout …)" in its section. (4) The full stderr is printed (keys redacted), not `tail -2`. (5) Both prompts tell the agent to write a draft report at minute 10, keep it updated, and the final at minute 17. (6) The presenter's profile name is just "Alex" (cycle-2 S3). The script now lives in the repo at `demo-loop/demo20b.sh` with env test seams (`DEMO_IDX`, `DEMO_WORK`, `DEMO_V2`, `DEMO_SERVE_LOG`, `DEMO_SKIP_SETUP`, `DEMO_AGENT_SECS`, `DEMO_STAGGER`, `DEMO_KILL_GRACE`), every default being the VM's real value.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the harness is one bash script with no pure functions to isolate; every rule is exercised through the script itself · integration `demo-loop/demo20b_test.ts` ("REQ-428 …", 5 tests: runs the real script with setup skipped and a fake `fleet-claude` (`demo-loop/testdata/fleet-claude`) on the PATH — status tags all `pair 6` for VM 5; both agents get `--output-format stream-json --verbose`; a no-report run shows "FINAL REPORT TEXT" and no `{"type":`; a hanging customer gets SIGTERM (its trap records `TERM`) before the hard timeout, its section says "killed by timeout", carries its last transcript event and all 3 stderr lines; both prompts ask for a minute-10 draft at their report path and the presenter is "Alex", not "Alex from DocuMonster" — the prompts are what the agents execute, so they get a content test) · e2e n/a — the end-to-end run is a 10-VM paid fleet; the integration test drives the whole script with only `claude` faked, and the transcript extractor was also run on a real `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose` transcript (final message "PONG"; with the result event removed it printed "[assistant] PONG").
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-harness-fixes off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first (seams-only commit, behaviour unchanged) — `deno test -A demo-loop/demo20b_test.ts` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 5 failed": `"[pair 5]" to match /\bpair 6\]$/`; the demoer args had no `--output-format`; raw `{"type":"result",…}` in the no-report section; the hung customer's section had no "killed by timeout" and only stderr lines 3 + "Terminated: 15"; the prompt had no minute-10 draft and named "Alex from DocuMonster". GREEN — the same file "ok | 5 passed | 0 failed"; `deno lint`, `deno check`, `deno fmt --check` clean on the test; `bash -n` clean on the script.
## REQ-418 — The model's job address is never a phone number, an email, or something nobody typed (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M27)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `M27` — "Client form prefills the phone number into the job address" (fleet-5 stdout:130-136: typed "Cotización rápida: reparar puerta de baño para Maria Lopez, 512-555-0199, $250"; the customer step's "Dirección del trabajo (opcional)" was prefilled with "512-555-0199"). RCA analyst LIKELY, skeptic UPHELD at `deb85b35`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked):** the deterministic `extractServiceAddress` finds no address in that sentence, so the value came from the model's `create_quote` argument `serviceAddress`. `backend/src/agents/domain/business/openai-tools/mod.ts` copied any non-empty string, and `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` preferred it over the extractor (`action.payload.serviceAddress?.trim() || extractServiceAddress(…)`); the quote stored it and AsstChat seeded `createAddress` from `quote.serviceAddress`. Introduced by 8c325610 (REQ-263).
**Requirement:** the address the user typed (the deterministic extractor, latest user turn first) wins. The model's `serviceAddress` is only a fallback, kept only when it is address-shaped — has letters, carries no phone number (NANP shapes; a ZIP+4 is not one) and no email — and grounded in a user turn: every number in it was typed, and at least one of its 3+-letter words was. The tool parser already drops a phone / email / letterless value. The tool's description (en + es) says "never a phone number or email". Helpers: `isAddressShaped`, `acceptModelServiceAddress` in `shared/quote-flow/quick-quote-prefill.ts`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/llm-address-guard.test.ts` ("REQ-418 …": the demo's exact sentence has no extractable address; phones in every shape, emails and letterless values are not address-shaped and never accepted; a ZIP+4 address is; an address nobody typed is dropped; a reworded typed one is kept; both dictionaries' tool description says "never a phone number or email") and `backend/src/agents/domain/business/openai-tools/test.ts` ("REQ-418 parseToolCall: a phone, email or letterless serviceAddress is left off") · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` ("REQ-418 …": the demo's exact sentence with the model returning "512-555-0199" / "Maria Lopez, 512-555-0199" stores no address; an invented "123 Main St" is not stored; the typed "412 Oak St Austin" wins over the model's "Oak St") · e2e n/a — the defect needs the real OpenAI model to emit the bad argument; the browser lane runs the stub LLM, which drafts no quote from free text. The integration test drives the real coordinator with the model's exact bad payload, and the prefill from `quote.serviceAddress` into the customer step is REQ-263's existing wiring.
**REQ-263 test amended:** "create_quote's serviceAddress is stored on the quote" typed "…at her place" while the model returned "412 Oak St, Austin TX" — an invented address, which REQ-418 now drops; the typed line is now "…at 412 oak st in austin, $350" (grounded, but lower case so the extractor can't read it), and the model's value is still stored.

## REQ-410 — A translation keeps every clause: no word budget, and a dropped exclusion is never cached as the customer's copy (demo-loop cycle 2, issue M24)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 2 (run r561db6d4, demo-report.md), issue `M24` — "Spanish translation dropped a contract exclusion (client-supplied faucets)": "60in double vanity, quartz top, 2 undermount sinks (faucets supplied by client / grifos los pone la clienta)" became "Mueble de baño de 60in, encimera de cuarzo, 2 lavabos bajo encimera" in the Spanish preview (fleet-6 stdout:182).
**Cause (RCA, analyst + skeptic UPHELD, at deb85b35):** `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-bullets/mod.ts:66` told the model to "keep each concise (3–8 words)" (from b6ec538e), so a 17-word line with a parenthetical exclusion was compressed and the exclusion went first. Only the line count and added money were checked (mod.ts:96-104); nothing checked that a clause survived, and TranslateQuote cached the short reply as the customer's `descriptionByLang.es`.
**Requirement:** the translate prompt has no length budget and says translate faithfully — never shorten, never drop parentheticals, exclusions, quantities or who-supplies-what. A code guard (`droppedLines`) flags any line whose source carries a parenthetical or an exclusion marker (supplied by, not included, excl, by client/owner, client-supplied, and the Spanish forms) when the translation is under 60% of the source's characters or lost its parenthetical; such a reply is retried once naming the lines, and a second short reply returns `translated:false` so the base text shows (with the UX-06 notice) and nothing is cached. Plain lines are not judged on length.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-bullets/mod.test.ts` ("REQ-410 M24 droppedLines …": the demo's faucet line flagged, a faithful one passes, un-parenthesised exclusions flagged in both directions, plain lines never judged) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-bullets/int.test.ts` ("REQ-410 M24 translate-bullets …": prompt has no 3–8 word budget and names parentheticals/exclusions/who-supplies; a shortening stub is retried once then returns the originals with `translated:false`; a faithful retry is used; an un-parenthesised exclusion cut short is refused; a plain line that translates shorter is trusted on the first call) · e2e n/a — the defect is the model's reply, which no browser lane can make the stub-LLM reproduce; the contract that `translated:false` is not cached and the base text shows is already covered by REQ-264's translate-quote int tests.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c2-translate-faithful off demo-fixes deb85b35):** RED first — `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-bullets/int.test.ts` → "FAILED | 6 passed | 4 failed" (prompt still "keep each concise (3–8 words)"; "one retry" expected 2 calls got 1; shortened faucet line returned as translated). ## REQ-444 — On Pick a price a question gets an answer and "add the permit" changes the job details; several changes in one message are all made, and the reply says what actually changed (demo-loop cycle 3, issue M21)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 3 (run re05e1cbb, `demo-loop/runs/re05e1cbb/demo-report.md`), issue `M21` — "The assistant ignores questions and says changes are done when they are not" (pair 7, fleet-6 stdout:141/194/209): on Pick a price "does this include the quartz slab material or just labor?? … ¿y el precio incluye el permiso de plomería? add permit if not" got only "Re-priced with your note — Competitive $17,000 · Market $20,000 · Premium $24,000." — no answer, no permit line. On Ready to send a mixed EN+ES fix that included "add a plumbing permit line $450" got "Done — the job details on the quote are updated."; the Spanish gained "Permiso de plomería", nothing was priced and the total stayed $20,000. RCA analyst CONFIRMED (medium), skeptic UPHELD, at cc5d4b0e.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked at cc5d4b0e):** (1) `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/mod.ts:993-1001` sent EVERY text typed on Pick a price to `repriceOnStep` (421-471), which re-runs SuggestPrices and answers with the fixed `priceStepReply` template (`chat-step/mod.ts:139-173`, `chatCoordinator.step.repriced`): no model read the question and nothing could change the job details. (2) `backend/src/agents/domain/data/openai/mod.ts:183-193` honoured only the FIRST tool call per turn ("the rest are dropped"), while `prompts.chatStep.review` asks for `update_job_details` AND `change_order` on such a message; and the `update_job_details` branch (mod.ts:1759-1761) replied with the fixed `chatCoordinator.jobDetailsUpdated` whenever the model wrote no prose, whatever had changed. (The dropped `change_order` of the 12:12:36 turn is inferred, not logged; the alternative — the model called `update_job_details` alone — ends in the same false "Done", which the reply rule below also closes.) Introduced by REQ-392 (f1d502fd) for the routing; the first-call-only rule dates from f0139414.
**Requirement:**
- On Pick a price the server classifies the text first (`priceStepIntent`, `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-step/mod.ts`). A question (`?` / `¿`, an interrogative opener, "is X included") or a change to the job ("add …", "agrega …", "include …", "remove …", "missing …") goes to the chat model with the job as typed, the job details on screen, the tiers on screen and what they include — the step hint now carries the tiers and their basis (`ChatStepHint.options` / `.basis`, `shared/quote-flow/step-composer.ts`) — and is offered only `update_job_details`, which on this step rewrites the job details on screen. The reply is the model's answer. When it changed the job details the reply says what changed (lines added / removed), the tiers are re-priced for the new details, and the reply carries `scope` (+ `scopeByLang`) so the island shows the new details and updates the confirmed option (a language it did not rewrite is dropped from the option, so the send translates it again). A message that asked for a change the model did not make says the job details are unchanged; a model that can't be reached is said so honestly. Only a price correction (no question, no change to the job) re-prices as before (REQ-392). A price named for the WHOLE job still fills the price box — never the price of an item being added ("add the permit, it's $450").
- `OpenAILLMClient.respond` returns EVERY valid tool call in the model's order (`LLMResponse.actions`; `action` stays the first) and names the calls whose arguments didn't parse (`dropped`). A tool the turn didn't offer is still never acted on and not reported (REQ-368).
- `HandleChatMessage` applies several changes to the quote in one turn, in order — `update_job_details` first, then each `change_order` / `revise_quote` as the model made them — and replies once, built from what actually changed: the job details' languages and added / removed lines, each line change's own reply, and the total's move. A job-details change that moved no price, on a message that named an amount, says the total is unchanged — never a bare "Done — …" (`chatCoordinator.jobDetailsUpdated` is gone). A mix that can't all run (a create / lock / terms call with others) runs the first call as before and the reply names what it didn't do; so does a call whose arguments didn't parse. `prompts.chatStep.review` asks for one tool call per change.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-step/price-ask.test.ts` (9, "REQ-444 priceStepIntent: …" / "REQ-444 priceStepContext: …": the demo's question goes to the chat model, never the re-pricer; '?', '¿…?', an interrogative opener and "is X included" are answered; add / include / remove / missing, English and Spanish, go to the chat model as a change to the job; REQ-392's own correction "No that's wrong, it's the WHOLE gut job … more like $28k" still re-prices and keeps $28,000 for the box; "add the permit, it's $450" never fills the price box while a job price named before the add does; the context carries the job as typed, the details on screen, the tiers with their rationale, what they include, a stated price — or that no tiers are on screen) · `backend/src/agents/domain/business/tool-calls/test.ts` (11, "REQ-444 toolCallsOf / planToolCalls / notDoneLine / jobDetailsChangeLine / jobDetailsChangeOf / totalMoveLine / pricesSameLine / sameJobDetails / workingTotalCents: …": every call the model made; several edits all run, the job details first, then the line changes in the model's order; one call stays on the single path; a mix keeps the first call and names the rest; the reply lines come from what changed — the languages, the lines added and removed, the total's move, or that no price changed) · `backend/src/agents/domain/data/openai/test.ts` (4, "REQ-444 OpenAILLMClient: …", a canned completion through the SDK's `fetch`, no network: both calls come back in order with `action` the first; an unparseable call is named in `dropped` and the valid one still comes back; only broken calls → no action, the text kept; a tool the turn did not offer is neither acted on nor reported) · `jest/unit/price-step-question.test.ts` (10, "REQ-444 …": `parseChatStepHint` keeps `options` / `basis` and drops junk, at most four tiers; `stepScopeOf`; `withStepScope` takes the new lines and drops a language the reply didn't rewrite, keeps one it did; every new string in both dictionaries, each in its own language; `chatCoordinator.jobDetailsUpdated` gone from both dictionaries and the coordinator;
