## REQ-699 — A quote can bill on a recurring schedule: a weekly / every-2-weeks / monthly payment term that signing turns into a Field subscription (demo-loop cycle 5, issue M20)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `M20` — "No monthly/recurring billing in the quote flow; Subscriptions not linked to quotes". Pair 2 typed "Cotización para María López, 305-555-0144, corte de césped y poda de setos, 4 visitas al mes, $180 al mes"; the payment step offered only one-off terms ("¿y cobro MENSUAL? No hay opción de mensual", fleet-1 stdout:406), the signature billed a one-time $180 (INV-001), and Campo → Suscripciones still said "0 ACTIVAS" (fleet-1 stdout:433). RCA analyst FEATURE_GAP (high), skeptic UPHELD, judge MISSING_IN_FLOW at demo-fixes `2444608a`. REQ-522 (cycle 3, m30) had already logged the quote→subscription half as a gap.
**Cause (RCA):** the payment step in `shared/quote-flow/wizard-terms.ts` offered only one-off schedules (due_now, net_15, 50_50, 30_30_40, deposit_bal, custom), and `SendSignedConfirmation` turned the pick into a fixed set of milestone invoices. A Subscription model existed only in the Field module (`backend/src/field/domain/data/field-stores/mod.ts` SubscriptionStore → the day's tasks → batch invoices), and nothing outside `backend/src/field` used it, so signing a quote could never start recurring billing. `shared/quote-flow/money-amounts.ts` already treated "$120 a month" as a recurring price, but nothing acted on it.
**Requirement:**
- The quote wizards' payment step (the generic one and the service-trade one; not the invoice wizard) offers **Recurring** / **Recurrente**. It opens a short form: how often (weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly), the amount per period (prefilled from the quote's total) and an optional end date. The term is stored in the English base as `Monthly · $180/mo`, `Weekly · $45/wk` or `Every 2 weeks · $90/2 wks`, with an optional ` · until YYYY-MM-DD`. Every reader localizes it: es `Mensual · $180/mes`, `Semanal · $45/semana`, `Cada 2 semanas · $90/2 semanas`, `… · hasta el 30 jun 2027`. The billing starts on the start-date term.
- `moneyAmounts` flags a price stated per period (`per`: weekly / biweekly / monthly / visit), e.g. "$180 al mes", "$180 a month", "$180/mo", "$45 a week", "$90 every 2 weeks", "$45 por visita". When the contractor's own words price the job that way, the payment step asks "You said $180 a month. Bill it once, or every month?" / "Dijiste $180 al mes. ¿Lo cobras una sola vez o cada mes?". One tap bills it on that schedule. The one-off options stay right there, and a per-visit price with no stated frequency opens the form instead.
- On the agreement (/q, the in-app preview and the PDF), the payment row reads the recurring term, and the payment schedule shows one row per period ("Monthly $180.00 · Billed every month"), never "Final payment on completion". `computePaymentSplit` never reads a recurring term as a percentage split.
- Signing a recurring quote creates no one-off milestone invoice. It creates ONE Field subscription linked to the quote (`quoteId`, `quoteNumber`) with the quote's customer, its job address (else the customer's address), one task type named after the job at the period amount, the cadence, the start day (never before the signing day), the optional end date (`isDue` is false after it) and the account's days to pay. The subscription is regrouped into a zone, so each period's visit lands on the day's round and, once done, the Field batch bills it (Field's own billing; no new cron). Creating it twice is a no-op. Paperwork reaches Field through a port (`QuoteSubscriptionPort`), because Field imports paperwork. If no subscription can be made (Field not booted, no customer), signing bills the period once, as before.
- `/field/subscriptions` and the customer card show the quote-linked subscription as "Monthly · $180/mo" / "Mensual · $180/mes", with the quote number. When the signature made that subscription (the public accept hands its id to the chat), the signed-quote chat line names the recurring charge and says it is billed from Field → Subscriptions; otherwise the line reads as before. The customer's confirmation email names the recurring charge.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/recurring-billing.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20 …": the term's base / parse / en+es text; money-amounts `per`; quote-facts' recurring prefill from pair 2's sentence; the wizard option and termFromPick's canonical value; computePaymentSplit never splits a recurring term; localizeTermValue; the en/es keys; the island, form, doc-parts, Field page and customer-card wiring), `front-end/lib/recurring-billing.test.tsx` ("REQ-699 …": doc-parts computeMilestones gives one recurring row in en/es), `backend/src/field/domain/business/quote-subscription/test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the subscription plan from a quote and its billing text) and `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-699 isDue stops after endDate") · integration `backend/src/field/domain/coordinators/field-quote-subscriptions/int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the port creates one linked, zoned subscription and is idempotent; a one-off quote makes none) `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/recurring.int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": a recurring quote bills no milestone invoice and asks the port; a non-recurring one never asks; no subscription → the period is billed once) and `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/signed-recurring.int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the agents + Field app over HTTP, the owner's thread ends on "María López firmó Q-001 · Mensual · $180/mes — se cobra desde Campo → Suscripciones" with no invoice on the row; recordSigned names Field's billing only when a subscription was made) · e2e `backend/src/field/entrypoints/quote-subscription.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20 e2e …", the app booted over HTTP: pair 2's monthly quote is signed on the public accept; no invoice is billed; GET /field/subscriptions holds the linked monthly subscription reading "Monthly · $180/mo" / "Mensual · $180/mes"; the first period's visit, completed and pulled by the Field batch, becomes a $180 invoice) and the browser stories `e2e/recurring-billing/recurring-billing.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20: …": pair 2's sentence in Spanish, the payment step asks "Dijiste $180 al mes. ¿Lo cobras una sola vez o cada mes?" next to the one-off options, "Cobrarlo cada mes" stores "Monthly · $180/mo", /q reads "Mensual · $180/mes" and "Se cobra cada mes", the public signature bills no invoice, Campo → Suscripciones reads "De Q-001 · Mensual · $180/mes" and the thread's divider says it is billed from there; and, with no price per period typed, Recurring from the options opens its form, and every 2 weeks, $90 and a last day store "Every 2 weeks · $90/2 wks · until 2027-06-30").

## REQ-710 — The English version of a Spanish-typed quote or invoice reads in English: the base language comes from the typed text, not the app language (demo-loop cycle 5, issue M4)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, `demo-loop/runs/r37f88707/demo-report.md`), issue `M4` — "The English version of a quote or invoice written in Spanish keeps the Spanish title and line items" (STILL PRESENT from cycle 4 M32): pair 6 (app in English, quote typed in Spanish, fleet-5 stdout:40/126/132/240/243) saw "Reparación de puerta de cocina $175.00" under English headings, the title "Carmen Núñez's Reparación de puerta Agreement" and the English subject "Quote Q-001 from Ortega Handyman Services — Reparación de puerta"; pair 9's English INV-002 (fleet-8 stdout:88/274) had a translated title over the line "Retiro de refrigerador y lavadora" and "PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS Zelle: +1 (512) 555-0108 · Efectivo" beside a "Cash" button; pair 7's English job details (fleet-6 stdout:90/217) read "Install kitchen backsplash 30 pies cuadrados subway tile". RCA analyst CONFIRMED (high), skeptic UPHELD, at 2444608a.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked in the worktree):** the quote's base language was the contractor's APP language, never the language of the text. "Lock it in" (`lock-quote/mod.ts:77,105`, `baseLang: me.language`) and the chat's lock branch (`handle-chat-message/mod.ts:3169`, `baseLang: replyLang` — `messageLang("lock it in")` is English) passed it to TranslateQuote, where the caller's word won (`translate-quote/mod.ts:195`); REQ-333 writes the base slots verbatim with no model call, so the typed Spanish became every English copy (`descriptionByLang.en`, each line's, `jobNameByLang.en`, `summaryByLang.en`), the model was asked for Spanish, `lang: "en"` was stored, and every English reader (the quote document, /q, the e-mail subject, the preview, the quote-linked invoice) showed the Spanish as English while the preview saw "nothing missing". TranslateInvoice (REQ-497) translated a standalone invoice's title and description, never its line items; the invoice stored its payment instructions as text frozen in the owner's language (`paymentInstructionsFromMethods`); the invoice e-mail and PDF drew a standalone invoice's title and concepts, and a quote-linked invoice's lines, as typed; and nothing checked a generated job-details line against its slot's language (pair 7). Introduced by 7cda0ef0 (REQ-333) and 9033db6e (REQ-497).
**Requirement:**
- A quote's base language is the language its own text reads in: `quoteTextLang` (`shared/quote-flow/quote-translations.ts`) — `messageLang` over the job name, summary, job details and every line item, each line's first capital lowered, a Spanish name's particles ("José de la Cruz", "Casa de la Rosa") not counted (`withoutNameParticles`, `shared/quote-flow/message-language.ts`). QuoteStore.create stamps it as `quote.lang`; TranslateQuote takes it first, then the caller's word, the stored `lang`, the app language, English. Lock and the chat's lock pass no base language.
- Repair: a quote whose stored `lang` disagrees with its text (`quoteLangStale`) is re-based by TranslateQuote — every per-language copy dropped, the base written verbatim, the other language translated; a failed model call still clears the wrong copies and the next run fills them. The send preview (PreviewQuoteSend) and the assistant preview (`previewTranslationMissing`) send a stale quote to the translator; the island takes the re-based `lang` from the reply.
- A standalone invoice's line items get `descriptionByLang` in the title's batch (TranslateInvoice; a batch invoice's visits, rendered by address, are left alone); its base language is read off its text the same way, the app language only a fallback; a PUT of the line items re-translates. `/invoices/:id/public` projects each line's copies while they still describe it (`invoiceLineItemsByLang`, `shared/documents/invoice-lang.ts`) and /i renders them through `localizeLineItems`.
- The invoice e-mail and PDF read the same copies: a standalone invoice's title and concepts (`invoiceTextByLang`), a quote-linked invoice's lines (`lineItemDescription` with the quote's base), in the document's language.
- Payment instructions read in the document's language at render time (`localizePaymentInstructions`, `shared/documents/invoice-form.ts`, on /i, the e-mail and the PDF): every " · " part or line that is a method's own label takes that label in the document's language; the details and the contractor's own words stay as typed.
- A generated job-details line (job name, summary, bullet) written in the other language for its slot — it reads as that language, or holds a unit or trade word only that language uses (`lineLangMismatch`) — is translated into the slot's language before the picker shows it (GenerateJobOptions: the picker and the chat-step rewrite); a failed fix keeps the line rather than dropping scope.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/c5-quote-base-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-710 …", 19: `quoteTextLang` — pair 6's quote reads Spanish, a line-initial capital is no name, an English quote with a Spanish customer name reads English, "José de la Cruz" / "María de los Santos" never make an English quote Spanish, too short → undefined; `quoteLangStale`; `previewTranslationMissing` true for the quote the old lock left; `lineLangMismatch` — "30 pies cuadrados" in English, "sq ft" in Spanish, a line in the other language, a name's particles, ordinary lines; `localizePaymentInstructions` — "· Efectivo" → "· Cash", every method's line round-trips, one method per line, free text untouched; `invoiceLineItemsByLang` — current copies projected, stale ones and no-`lang` ones dropped; the assistant island takes the re-based `lang` from the translate reply — a source check of `AsstChat.tsx`) · `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/base-lang.test.ts` (5: Spanish typed in an English account stamped `es`, English in a Spanish account `en`, the text over a caller's `lang`, too short → nothing, José de la Cruz never `es`) · `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/base-lang.test.ts` (3: pair 9's INV-002 e-mail in English — English title, concepts and "· Cash"; ## REQ-333 AMENDMENT (REQ-710, demo-loop cycle 5, M4) — the base language is the language the quote's text reads in
REQ-333's order for TranslateQuote's base language — "the caller's word (lock passes the contractor's app language …), else the quote's stored `lang`, else the contractor's `user.language`, else `en`" — is replaced: the language the quote's own text reads in (`quoteTextLang`) first, then the caller's word, the stored `lang`, the app language, English; QuoteStore.create stamps that language on the quote, and lock and the chat's lock pass no base language. A quote stored with a base its text disagrees with is re-based (REQ-710). REQ-333's rule itself — the base language is never sent to the model and its slots are the typed text — is unchanged. **Tests:** REQ-710's (above); REQ-333's own tests in `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-quote/int.test.ts` and `lock-quote/int.test.ts` stay green unchanged — their text ("Bathroom remodel", "Demo and haul-off") is too short to tell, so the caller's word and the stored language still decide there.

## REQ-497 AMENDMENT (REQ-710, demo-loop cycle 5, M4) — a standalone invoice's lines are translated too, from the language it was typed in
TranslateInvoice's base language is read off the invoice's own text first; the caller's word (the app language) and the stored `lang` decide only when the text can't tell. Its line items ride the title's batch (`lineItems[i].descriptionByLang`, the base slot the cache key; a batch invoice's visits excluded), a PUT of the line items re-translates them, and the public projection, the e-mail and the PDF read the per-language title, concepts and lines while they still describe the typed text. **Tests:** REQ-710's (above); REQ-497's in `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-invoice/int.test.ts` and `http.int.test.ts` stay green unchanged.

## REQ-715 — A customer carries the language they read; every send to them, and their /q /i /co pages, start in it (demo-loop cycle 5, issues m31 + c2-M29 + c3-m43 + c4-M34)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m31` — "No per-client language" (pair 6: "¿cómo le digo que Carmen habla español? No veo campo de idioma del cliente."), merged with the backlog items `c2-M29` "Customer has no language setting; Message is only an sms: link", `c3-m43` "A client has no language preference" and `c4-M34` "No per-client language preference; assistant doesn't remember it". RCA analyst FEATURE_GAP (high), skeptic UPHELD at `2444608a`; judge MISSING_IN_FLOW for all four.
**Cause (RCA):** `backend/src/crm/dto/customer.ts` had no language field, so nothing could record that Carmen reads Spanish. Every send resolved its language as the per-send pick → the account's `commsLanguage` → en (`shared/quote-flow/comms-language.ts`), and the reminder, receipt, change-order and signed-confirmation dispatchers read `identity.commsLanguage` directly (`send-payment-reminder/mod.ts:152` `biz?.commsLanguage === "es" ? "es" : "en"`). Both send dialogs started "Sends in" on the app language; `/q` opened in English unless the visitor chose a language; `/i` and `/co` fell back to the contractor's default; and the assistant had nowhere to put "Ella habla español".
**Requirement:** A customer has an optional `language` (`"en" | "es"`). It is set in the /customers New customer form ("Customer's language" / "Idioma del cliente": Not set / English / Español, with a hint), changed in place on the card (a select row that saves on pick through `PUT /customers/:id`; "Not set" clears it), and set for the New invoice modal's inline new client. `POST` / `PUT /customers` accept en | es ("" clears it on edit and stores nothing on create) and refuse anything else with a 400. `resolveCommsLanguage` takes the customer's language between the per-send pick and `identity.commsLanguage`. Every customer-facing dispatcher resolves through it once the document's customer is known: quote and invoice email and text (paid included), the send preview, SendQuote's recorded `lastDelivery.lang` (for the published quote's customer), overdue reminders (their link carries `?lang=`), payment receipts (email, PDF, and a text link with `?lang=`), change-order requests (`/co/<id>?lang=`), the signed confirmation (email + countersigned PDF) and the field texts to a customer (service canceled, moved, on today's schedule). A per-send pick still wins. UX-28's adopt-the-first-pick rule never makes a pick that is only the customer's own language the account default (`commsLanguageToAdopt`). Both send dialogs (the /quotes panel and the assistant's review card) start "Sends in" on the customer's language (`defaultSendLang`; the review card's "Preview in" follows it until the contractor taps a pill) and offer it even when it is not one of the account's send languages (`sendLangChoices`). ## REQ-727 — /invoices never sends an invoice at once: Issue / Finish + send / Send now open a send sheet with the channel, the invoice's language and what they'll get (demo-loop cycle 5, issue c4-M16 / m56)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `c4-M16` "Invoices go out at once: no preview, confirmation or channel choice" (the merged report's m56, "'Finish + send' sends at once with no review"; fleet-r37f88707-7/stdout:311: "/invoices > 'Finish + send →' sent at once (no review/confirm step)"). Judge: MISSING_IN_FLOW, still present at demo-fixes `2444608a`.
**Cause (RCA):** `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` sent the moment a button was pressed. The card CTA `ctaAction` → `doFinishDraft` / `doSendNow` → `dispatchInvoice` POSTed /invoices/:id/email AND /text with no body; New invoice `submit(true)` and "Send INV-001 now" (`sendPrior`) did the same. There was no dialog, no preview and no channel choice, while a quote goes through `QuoteSendDialog` (QuotesPage.tsx:64) with the channel, "Sends in" and "What they'll get". The invoice email/text routes took no language either, so a send could only go out in the Settings default.
**Requirement:**
- On /invoices, "Finish + send" (Drafting), "Send now" (Upcoming), "Issue invoice" (New invoice, client reachable) and "Send INV-001 now" (New invoice's earlier bill) send nothing by themselves. Each opens the invoice send sheet: the quote's send dialog (`SendDialog`, components/QuoteSendDialog.tsx, on lib/send-dialog.ts's rules) for the invoice. It reads "How do you want to send INV-001 to Juan Perez?" and offers Text + Email / Text / Email. Recommended and "needs an email" follow what is on file: the customer's live record, else the invoice's bill-to, which is what the send endpoints use. A missing contact is asked for in the sheet. "Sends in" starts on the invoice's own language: its typed language, else the language its quote went out in, else the Settings default. "What they'll get" shows the real email subject and body and the text, from `GET /invoices/:id/send-preview`, rendered by the send's own renderers with the dates the send will stamp. The preview sends nothing.
- Only the sheet's Send dispatches, on the picked channel(s) only, in the picked language (`POST /invoices/:id/email|text` now take `{ language }`). A one-channel send that fails names that channel only. Cancel sends nothing: a card stays where it was, and an invoice that "Issue invoice" just created stays a draft while the page says "INV-001 saved as a draft — not sent".

## REQ-730 — the /field/* list pages paint their rows in the first HTML, not a "Loading…" line waiting for hydration (demo-loop cycle 5, issue c2-p13-p)

Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — and, for this run, "we want to fix what we have identified as bug, polish or breaking."

Demo issue **c2-p13-p** (cycle 2 backlog, judged BUG_POLISH in cycle 5, RCA at 2444608a): "Brief 'Loading…' lines flash". Every `/field/*` route server-rendered its island with no data (`routes/field/workers.tsx` → `<FieldWorkersPage />`), and the island fetched its lists in a mount `useEffect` (`islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx:98`), so the first HTML and the hydrated page showed a `field.common.loading` text line (`:457`) before the rows replaced it. The same held for assignments, subscriptions, batches and tasks.

Requirement: the field routes (`workers`, `assignments`, `subscriptions`, `batches`, `tasks`) read their first lists on the SSR side with the caller's session (`front-end/lib/field-ssr.ts`, the REQ-471 pattern) and pass them to the island as `seed`. A seeded island renders its rows on its first render and makes no mount fetch. A list that can't be read gives `null`, and the island fetches on hydration as before. `/field/tasks` seeds the server's day and the island uses it only when the browser's day is the same one.

**Tests:**
- unit `front-end/lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` ("REQ-730 (c2-p13-p) …"): each loader reads its paths with the session and returns null for no session or an unreadable/thrown main list; failed side reads fall back. Each seeded island (Workers, Assignments, Subscriptions, Batches, Tasks) renders its row (`wk-row`, `asg-region`, `subs-card`, `lt-past`, `tk-task`) with no "Loading…"/"Cargando…" line on its first render, and the unseeded Workers page still shows it. Every route calls its loader and passes `seed={seed}`. `jest/unit/c4-batch-checks-note-flash.test.ts` (REQ-608) now anchors on the mount effect's `load()` call, because the effect returns early when seeded.
- integration: n/a. No backend or wire change; the endpoints are the ones the islands already read, and the e2e below proves the SSR join against the real backend.
- e2e `e2e/field-ssr-first-paint/field-ssr-first-paint.e2e.test.ts`: (1) a signed-in owner with a worker gets a raw server answer for `/field/workers` that carries `data-cy="wk-row"` and the worker's name, with no browser and no JS, and none of the five `/field/*` pages contains "Loading…" or "Cargando…". (2) After a pull, the raw `/field/batches` HTML lists the batch and carries its draft's `lt-check` already ticked.

**Evidence (2026-11-12, Mac host, branch fix/c5-field-ssr-lists off demo-fixes 2444608a):**
- RED first. `deno test -A --no-check lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` with the loaders stubbed gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 10 failed" ("not implemented"; "AssertionError: a worker row is in the first HTML" / "a zone…" / "a card…" / "a past batch…" / "a task…"; "workers: the route calls loadFieldWorkersSeed("). With the loaders done and the islands at HEAD, the five render tests still failed on those same row assertions. `shots run e2e/field-ssr-first-paint` gave "✗ REQ-730 … expectation failed: the first HTML of /field/workers carries the worker row".
- GREEN. `deno test -A lib/field-ssr.test.tsx lib/field-map.test.ts lib/field.test.ts lib/quotes-ssr.test.tsx` gave "ok | 29 passed | 0 failed". `shots run e2e/field-ssr-first-paint` gave ✓ for both REQ-730 stories.
- Neighbours. jest unit project: "Test Suites: 392 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed". `deno lint`, `deno check` and `deno fmt --check` are clean on every touched file. Browser stories, run in small batches because the host load average was 100–180: ✓ REQ-421 (field-worker-errors), ✓ REQ-365 (field-oneoff-zone), ✓ REQ-608 "pulled batch's drafts still ticked after a reload" (run alone), and ✓ REQ-143/144/145/152/157/159/163 (field-tasks).

## REQ-726 — the topbar activity pill is a short-lived notice out of the search row, and its link lands on Activity (demo-loop cycle 5, issues m6 + m57)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issues m6 "Toasts/top-bar notice stay for minutes and squeeze the search box" and m57 "Activity toast link doesn't scroll to Activity". RCA at 2444608a: m6 CONFIRMED (skeptic UPHELD), m57 CONFIRMED (skeptic CORRECTED).
**Cause (RCA):** m6: `DashTopbar` rendered `newestNotification(items)` whenever any notification existed. Nothing expired it, so "Pago registrado … hace 4m" sat on every page. `TOPBAR_CSS` hid the pill only at ≤1249px, so at 1280 and 1440 it shared the row with the greeting, the search and EN/ES. The search placeholder was cut, the sentence was clamped and the monospace time wrapped. m57: the pill links to `/dashboard#activity`, but the `DashboardPage` island's SSR render is the skeleton, so the parsed HTML has no `#activity` and the browser's fragment scroll finds nothing. The panel mounts later (at hydration on a warm start, after the fetch on a cold one), and nothing scrolled to it. The first-visit coach mark covered the page.
**Requirement:**
- The pill shows the newest event only while it is younger than 90 s (`TICKER_LIFETIME_MS`, `freshTickerItem` in `front-end/lib/ticker-pick.ts`). The 3.8 s age tick re-evaluates it, so it then goes away. An older event never stands in for it, and the Activity panel keeps the history.
- It is hidden below 1500px (`TOPBAR_CSS`), so it never shares the search row at 1280 or 1440.
- `.topbar__ticker-time` stays on one line in the body font. This supersedes REQ-542's wrap. The pill's floor is now 240px, so a one-line "ahora mismo" fits.
- On `/dashboard#activity` the island scrolls the Activity panel into view (`scrollToHashTarget`, `front-end/lib/dash-anchor.ts`), once it mounts and again when the lists land. The coach mark skips that arrival without persisting, so a later plain visit still teaches the assistant.
- Amended pins: REQ-406's 1249px test now accepts a higher breakpoint, REQ-319's source test accepts `freshTickerItem`, and REQ-542's "time may wrap" assertion is dropped. The pill-visible e2e stories (REQ-273/319/406/476/488/496/542) and cypress UX-21 now run at ≥1500px, and UX-21 uses a fresh stubbed event.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/topbar-ticker-expiry.test.ts` ("REQ-726 m6 …" ×8, "REQ-726 m57 …" ×4) · integration n/a: front-end only, with no backend or wire change. The notifications feed is unchanged. · e2e `e2e/topbar-ticker-expiry/topbar-ticker-expiry.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-726 m6 …": pill hidden at 1280/1440 with the search placeholder whole, time on one line at 1600, a 4-minute-old event not shown; "REQ-726 m57 …": cold and warm `/dashboard#activity` scroll `.content` to the panel, with no coach mark).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-topbar-ticker off demo-fixes 2444608a):**

## REQ-714 — a signed-in worker's /worker page renders in the worker's language on the server — no English first paint (demo-loop cycle 5, m58) (2026-11-12)

The user: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), issue **m58** — "worker view flashes English first" (BUG_POLISH, RCA CONFIRMED + skeptic UPHELD at 2444608a): `routes/worker/index.tsx` picked the SSR language from `?lang=`, the pm_worker_lang pick or the browser's pm_lang only, never the worker's session, so a Spanish worker on an English browser saw English until the island's `workerClient.me()` returned and REQ-285 flipped it to Spanish.

- With a `pm_worker` cookie, the route reads the worker on the server (GET /field/worker/me, as the island does; in-process on Deno Deploy, BACKEND_URL in dev) via `front-end/lib/worker-ssr.ts` `loadWorkerLang`, and renders in the worker's language unless `?lang=` (REQ-285) or the /worker pick (REQ-494) chose one. No cookie → no backend call; signed out or a failing backend → the old order.
- `workerRouteLang` also returns `pageLang` (the page's own, without the worker); the island gets it so Salir still returns to it and the worker's language is never written into the browser's pm_lang (REQ-416).
- The Spanish default for new workers (REQ-155, REQ-520) is unchanged; whether an English-only account should default new workers to English is left to the owner.

**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts` (REQ-714 workerRouteLang with a worker, readWorkerCookie, loadWorkerLang, the route + island wiring); updated `front-end/lib/worker-lang-pick.test.ts`, `jest/unit/worker-lang-session.test.ts` (REQ-416 source check follows `pageLang ?? initialLang`).
- integration: `backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-ssr-lang.int.test.ts` — `loadWorkerLang` against the real FieldWorkerController (Spanish worker on an English browser → es; English worker → en; no cookie / signed out → null).
- e2e: `e2e/worker-language/worker-language.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-714 m58: a signed-in Spanish worker on an English browser gets a Spanish page from the server" — server HTML has `<html lang="es">` and the Spanish title; pm_lang stays en. Written, not run here (the browser lane is out of scope for this fix pass).

**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-worker-lang-ssr off demo-fixes 2444608a):** RED on the original field.ts / WorkerScreen.tsx / route — `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts` → "FAILED | 3 passed | 2 failed": workerRouteLang gave `lang: "en"` (expected `"es"`, `pageLang: "en"`) for a Spanish worker on an English browser; "the route asks the backend" failed. GREEN — `deno test -A lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts lib/worker-lang-pick.test.ts lib/ssr-lang.test.ts` → "ok | 16 passed | 0 failed"; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/entrypoints/` → "ok | 36 passed | 0 failed" (incl. the REQ-714 int test); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 392 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed"; deno lint, deno check and deno fmt --check clean on every touched file.

## REQ-732 — Escape closes every dialog on the shared Backdrop (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m26)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m26` "Escape and backdrop click don't close dialogs" (BUG_POLISH): fleet-1 stdout:328 "Escape does not close it; the backdrop kept blocking clicks until I pressed Cancelar" on New invoice and Nueva suscripción.
**Cause (RCA, analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic CORRECTED, at demo-fixes 2444608a):** `front-end/components/Backdrop.tsx` (REQ-354) wired only `onPointerDown`/`onClick` through `createBackdropGuard`; Escape was per-dialog and opt-in. ClientsPage's New customer (REQ-289, its own document keydown listener), ClientsBoard's card and EndDemo had one; New invoice (`InvoicesPage.tsx` NewInvoiceModal) and Nueva suscripción (`FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`) did not — and the subscription form's line search (`onComboKey`) stopped every Escape, open or not. The backdrop-click half was "plausible but unproven"; the e2e below shows a deliberate backdrop click does close both dialogs.
**Requirement:** every dialog on `<Backdrop>` closes on Escape. Open Backdrops form a stack (`createEscapeLayers` / `documentEscapeLayers` in `front-end/lib/backdrop-dismiss.ts`) with one document `keydown` listener: only the topmost dialog closes; an Escape a nested list already handled (`defaultPrevented`, or stopped before the document), one ending an IME composition, and other keys close nothing; a handled Escape is `preventDefault()`ed. Escape runs the Backdrop's `onEscape` when given, else `onClose` — so busy guards hold (New invoice `!busy`, Settings reset `!resetBusy`, work orders `!busy`). ClientsPage's own listener is removed: its Backdrop's `onEscape={() => !adding && setAddOpen(false)}` closes even a dirty draft (REQ-300: "Cancel / Escape still close it, and the draft is kept"). SearchSelect stops an Escape only while its list is open; the subscription line search only while its search is open.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx` ("REQ-732 m26 …" ×8: Escape closes the one dialog and marks it handled; only the topmost closes; handled / composing / other keys close nothing; one listener while open, none after; out-of-order unmounts; a mounted `<Backdrop>` (preact render on deno-dom) closes on Escape, prefers `onEscape`, stops after unmount; ClientsPage has no own keydown listener and its Backdrop's `onEscape` closes unless saving; SearchSelect and the line search stop Escape only while open), `front-end/lib/form-a11y.test.tsx` (REQ-289's pin now reads the Backdrop's `onEscape`) · integration n/a — front-end keyboard behaviour only, no server path changes · e2e `e2e/backdrop-escape/backdrop-escape.e2e.test.ts` (en and es: New invoice closes on Escape, also with the focus in a field, and on a backdrop click; Nueva suscripción closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, and an Escape that shuts the open customer list leaves it up until the next Escape).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-backdrop-escape off demo-fixes 2444608a):** RED — `deno test -A --no-check lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx` → "SyntaxError: … does not provide an export named 'createEscapeLayers'"; with a no-op stub export: "FAILED | 1 passed | 7 failed" ("Escape calls onClose", "ClientsPage still registers its own keydown listener", "SearchSelect: an Escape that closes the open list must not also close the dialog"). `shots run e2e/backdrop-escape/backdrop-escape.e2e.test.ts` against `PORT=20508 deno task serve` → all four ✗ "timed out: New invoice closes on Escape" / "timed out: Nueva suscripción closes on Escape". GREEN — `deno test -A lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx lib/backdrop-dismiss.test.ts lib/backdrop-overlays.test.ts lib/form-a11y.test.tsx lib/sb-drawer.test.tsx` → "ok | 28 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/backdrop-escape e2e/backdrop-dblclick e2e/form-a11y` → "9 pass · 0 fail" (REQ-732 ×4, REQ-354 ×2, REQ-289 ×3); `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint` on the 7 touched files and `deno check` on them plus every other Backdrop island clean; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 392 passed, 392 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed, 3850 total".
